docs.title: Vault schema
docs.text: Rules for the docs/ vault, the project's second brain. It follows the LLM-wiki pattern (immutable sources, maintained notes, a schema), adapted so every note also reads correctly on GitHub. python scripts/docs_vault.py lint checks the mechanical rules and runs in CI.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text: Layer Where Rule Sources The code, testosterone.yaml, CHANGELOG.md, merged pull requests The source of truth. Notes describe it and never override it Notes Every folder under docs/ except Archive/ Maintained. They describe the code as it is today Archive docs/Archive/ Frozen. Dated plans, audits and checklists; fix a broken link, never the content Schema This file Changes when the conventions change

docs.title: Special files
docs.text: File Role Index The one entry point. Every note is reachable from it, directly or through its folder's hub note Log Append-only record of vault operations, newest last Agent Context Guide Which note to read before changing what

docs.title: Frontmatter
docs.text:
Every note starts with:

---
type: index | schema | log | architecture | reference | guide | spec | roadmap | tracker | archive
status: current | archived
created: YYYY-MM-DD
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
---
  • updated changes whenever the body changes. CI fails a pull request that edits a note and leaves the date alone.
  • status: archived is for notes under Archive/, and only those.
  • Extra keys (tags, related, title) are allowed.

docs.title: Writing rules
docs.text:
• One copy of a fact. Link to the note that owns it. Per-change history belongs in CHANGELOG.md, not in notes.
  • No fact that can rot silently. A statement is either how the code works now, or carries its date or version ("removed in v1.1").
  • Links are relative markdown links with spaces encoded as %20. No [[wikilinks]]; they do not render on GitHub.
  • No orphans. A new note is linked from Index or its folder's hub note in the same change.
  • Notes are short. Facts and structure, with a pointer to the code.

docs.title: Ingest: every pull request
docs.text:
1. List what the change alters: CLI flags, exit codes, testosterone.yaml keys, engine flow, API, CI, release steps.
  2. Find the notes that own those facts through the Agent Context Guide and update them in the same pull request. Bump updated.
  3. A design decision gets a note under Specs & ADRs/, linked from its README.
  4. A note that stops describing the code moves to Archive/ with type: archive and status: archived, and is linked from the Archive README.
  5. Run python scripts/docs_vault.py lint.

A pull request that changes none of those facts needs no note change.

docs.title: Query
docs.text: Start at Index, follow links, then check the code the note points to. If the answer was missing from the vault, add it to the note that should have had it.

docs.title: Lint
docs.text: python scripts/docs_vault.py lint checks frontmatter, broken links, wikilinks and orphans. Contradictions between notes and stale claims need a reader: when you find one, fix it and add a line to the Log.

docs.title: Log
docs.text: Add an entry to log.md when the vault itself changes shape: notes added, moved, archived or merged, a lint pass, a schema change. Format: ## YYYY-MM-DD: <operation> and one or two lines. Routine note updates that ride along with a code change are not logged; the changelog and git history cover them.

docs.title: Sync
docs.text:
• GitHub is the copy of record. Notes change through pull requests.
  • Local Obsidian vault is the docs/ folder of a checkout. It shows whatever that checkout has pulled, so run git pull --ff-only origin main to see merged changes.
  • GitHub wiki is generated from docs/ by .github/workflows/wiki-sync.yml on every push to main that touches the vault. Never edit the wiki; the next sync overwrites it.

docs.title: Compared with other tools
docs.text:
Index · Getting Started

Testosterone keeps the history of your test runs and tells you what changed: what broke, what's flaky and what got slower. It does that for any runner that writes JUnit XML (or that it can run itself), as a pip install on a laptop or one container for a team, with no account and no per-seat bill. This page says where that fits next to the tools teams already know, and when one of them is the better choice.

Features and prices of the other tools change often. This page describes them as of October 2026, from their own docs; check theirs before you decide.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: Testosterone Allure Report ReportPortal Currents Trunk Flaky Tests Datadog Test Optimization Hosting Your machine or your server Static files Your server (several services) or their cloud Their cloud Their cloud Their cloud Price Free, MIT Free Free self-hosted; paid cloud Paid, by usage Free tier, then paid Paid, part of Datadog Runners Any that writes JUnit XML, plus pytest, Behave, BehaveX and Playwright adapters Most, through Allure adapters Most, through agents Playwright, Cypress Most, through JUnit upload Most, through Datadog libraries History across runs Yes, with per-test diffs between any two runs One run, with an optional history folder Yes Yes Yes Yes Flaky test detection Yes, plus quarantine in config Retries only Yes Yes Yes Yes Per-test history page Yes: outcomes, flake rate over time, duration, owner Per run Yes Yes Yes Yes Traces, screenshots and videos Playwright attachments on the test page Yes, the richest per-run view Yes Yes, streamed live Not its focus Through Datadog APM Runs the tests for you Yes (testo run, cycles of stages) No No Orchestrates Playwright and Cypress No No Test case management and manual testing No No (Allure TestOps does) No No No No

docs.title: When to pick something else
docs.text:
• You want the richest report for a single run. Allure Report's per-run view (steps, retries, attachments) is deeper than Testosterone's. They work together: Testosterone can write Allure reports as one of its reporters and link to them from each run.
  • You need test case management or manual testing. That's Allure TestOps, Testmo and similar tools. Testosterone only knows about tests that ran.
  • You want failures sorted automatically, with ML, across a large organisation. ReportPortal's auto-analysis learns from past decisions. Testosterone remembers a cause someone marked and applies it to failures with the same message, which is simpler and easier to predict, but it doesn't guess.
  • You run Playwright or Cypress at scale and want CI load balancing. Currents splits and orders specs across machines and streams results live. Testosterone records what ran; it doesn't schedule specs across CI machines.
  • Your team already lives in Datadog. Datadog Test Optimization links tests to traces, deploys and test impact analysis. Testosterone can send each run to Datadog as an OpenTelemetry trace (testo otel) and pick the tests a change can affect (testo affected), but it doesn't link test spans to your services' traces.

docs.title: When Testosterone fits
docs.text:
• Test data can't leave your network, or you don't want another SaaS and another per-seat bill.
  • You use more than one runner (pytest, Playwright, Behave, a shell script) and want them in one history.
  • You want "what changed since main" on every pull request without wiring up a hosted service: one CI step with the GitHub Action, or pytest --testo on your own machine.
  • You want to try it in minutes: pip install testo-core, testo ingest results.xml, testo ui. The Getting Started guide has the details, and the live demo's try-it page reads a JUnit file in your browser with nothing installed.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Add Testosterone to a project you already have, in about five minutes: install it, describe your tests in one file, run them, see what changed, then run the same thing in GitHub Actions. Every command below was run against testo-core 1.1.1 from PyPI in a fresh virtualenv.

You need Python 3.11 or newer and a project with tests. The examples use pytest; other runners are at step 6.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install testo-core pytest
testo --version          # testo 1.x.y

testo-core is the testo CLI. It doesn't install your test runner, so keep installing pytest (or Behave, Jest...) the way your project already does.

docs.title: 2. Describe your tests
docs.text:
Create testosterone.yaml in the project root. A cycle is a named list of stages; each stage runs one test command.

version: 1
cycles:
  unit:
    description: My unit tests.
    stages:
      - name: unit
        equipment: pytest
        args: [-q, tests]

Check it:

testo config validate    # ok — version=1 cycles=1 ...
testo doctor             # config, runners on PATH, database

For autocomplete in VS Code and other editors, put the $schema line at the top of the file.

testo config init writes a starter file with a smoke-test cycle that runs pytest -q tests, plus commented-out marker-based pytest and BehaveX examples. Edit its args if your tests live outside tests/.

docs.title: 3. Run it
docs.text:
testo run --cycle unit

You get a panel per stage, a summary table (total, passed, failed, skipped) and the exit code: 0 when everything passed, 1 when a test failed. All exit codes are in Troubleshooting and Error Codes.

Each run is recorded in testo_history.db (SQLite, next to the config) with its logs under artifacts/ and a per-run copy of its reports under .testo/ (set TESTO_HOME to put that elsewhere). Add all three to .gitignore.

docs.title: 4. See what changed
docs.text:
Break a test and run the cycle again, then ask for the difference between the last two runs:

testo run --cycle unit       # exit 1
testo summary --cycle unit

Quality score (pass / total)
  Baseline 100.0%  →  50.0%  Δ -50.0 pp
Regressions & risk
  Kind         Test       Before   After
  regression   test_sub   passed   failed

Once a cycle has a few runs, testo flaky --cycle unit lists tests that keep flipping between pass and fail.

testo report list shows every recorded run and testo diff <BASELINE_ID> <CURRENT_ID> compares any two. How deltas are classified is in Delta Comparison Policy.

docs.title: 5. Run it in GitHub Actions
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/tests.yml
name: tests
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - run: pip install pytest            # your project's test dependencies
      - uses: taltal-beep/testosterone@v1
        with:
          cycle: unit
          python-version: "3.11"         # same Python as above, so it sees your dependencies

The action installs testo-core, runs testo run --ci (one JSON event per line in the log), writes the results to the job summary and fails the job when the cycle fails. Add comment-on-pr: "true" (and pull-requests: write permission) to get the same summary as a comment on each pull request. Its inputs and outputs, and the GitLab CI template, are in CI-CD Pipeline Setup.

docs.title: 6. Add other test runners
docs.text:
Add stages to the same cycle; they run in order.

    stages:
      - name: unit
        equipment: pytest
        args: [-q, tests]
      - name: flows
        equipment: behave
        args: [features/smoke.feature]     # always name the feature files; needs testo-core[bdd]
      - name: web
        equipment: command                 # any runner that writes JUnit XML
        args: [npx, jest, --ci]
        junit_xml: ["reports/junit/*.xml"]

behave and behavex stages need the bdd extra: pip install 'testo-core[bdd]' (in the GitHub Action, package: "testo-core[bdd]").

Every key (timeouts, workers, triggers on changed paths, reporters such as Allure) is in Command Reference. A runner or reporter that isn't built in can come from a plugin package.

docs.title: Already have CI? Record its results instead
docs.text:
If your tests already run somewhere, skip the YAML and add one step after them. Any runner that writes JUnit XML works (JUnit5, pytest's --junitxml, PHPUnit, ...), and so do the files Jest, Vitest, Playwright, dotnet test, go test -json, Robot Framework, RSpec, k6 and Xcode (xcresulttool) write themselves, or an allure-results folder. Prefer the runner's own format when it has one: Jest's --json report keeps a test file that failed to compile, while jest-junit drops it and names every suite undefined.

pip install testo-core
testo ingest 'reports/**/*.xml' --cycle web-unit

The run gets the same history, testo summary, testo flaky and Compare as a testo run. For one history across every CI job and teammate, run the Team Server and add --server https://your-server --token "$TESTO_API_TOKEN". Which file each runner writes: Command Reference § testo ingest.

docs.title: Using pytest? One flag
docs.text:
pip install testo-core
pytest --testo                       # or --testo-cycle api-unit to name the cycle

Every run is recorded like testo ingest would record it (the cycle defaults to the project folder's name), with the checkout's branch and commit, so testo ui shows what broke since the last run on your branch. Without the flag the plugin does nothing. Details: Command Reference § pytest --testo.

docs.title: Changelog Generation and CI Enforcement Policy
docs.text: CHANGELOG.md (repo root) follows Keep a Changelog: an ## [Unreleased] section plus dated ## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD sections, paired with the project's semver (pyproject.toml / frontend/package.json).

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
Two independent CI checks, both required on PRs:

  • commitlint (.github/workflows/commitlint.yml) — lints commit messages in a PR against commitlint.config.js (@commitlint/config-conventional, no overrides; the repo's existing feat:/fix:/test: commits already conform).
  • changelog_required (a job inside .github/workflows/ci.yml, the unified format -> test -> deploy pipeline) — fails a PR that changes non-doc files without also touching CHANGELOG.md. Escape hatch: apply the no-changelog label for PRs that don't warrant an entry (same idiom pr-heavy.yml uses for its e2e-heavy label).

docs.title: AI auto-changelog on main
docs.text:
.github/workflows/changelog-on-main.yml triggers on every push to main and uses anthropics/claude-code-base-action to read the pushed commit range and draft an entry under ## [Unreleased], then commits the result directly to main, with no PR review step. This was a deliberate choice, not an oversight — the tradeoff:

  • Known risk: AI-authored content lands on main unreviewed. A bad summary, or one that misattributes a change, ships without a human catching it first.
  • Mitigations: the workflow runs scripts/check_changelog_format.py after the AI edit and refuses to push if the file is structurally broken (missing [Unreleased] heading, malformed version heading); the AI's tool access is scoped to read/edit CHANGELOG.md only, plus read-only git log/git diff; and ## [Unreleased] stays human-editable right up until the next real version is cut, so a bad entry can be fixed before it's ever attached to a release.
  • Loop prevention (three independent layers — verify all three still hold if any one is touched): paths-ignore: [CHANGELOG.md] on the trigger, a job-level if: github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]' guard, and [skip ci] in the bot's own commit message.

docs.title: Prerequisites (GitHub repo settings, not files)
docs.text:
• Secret CHANGELOG_BOT_TOKEN — a PAT/App token for an identity allowed to push past branch protection on main (the default GITHUB_TOKEN cannot).
  • Secret ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for the Claude Code action.
  • main branch protection updated to let that bot identity bypass "require pull request before merging."
  • commitlint and changelog_required added to the branch protection rule's required status checks.

docs.title: Backfill
docs.text: The initial ## [0.1.0] entry was backfilled from the four completed development phases, sourced from the phase release checklists (now in docs/Archive/) cross-referenced with git log, so 0.1.0 covers everything shipped up to then rather than being split across invented historical releases.

docs.title: Engine and CLI bug hunt, 2026-10-31
docs.text:
A hands-on pass over the Python side: testo commands, testosterone.yaml parsing, the engine (testo_core/engine/), storage and history, resource leases and the result importers behind testo ingest. Everything below was reproduced by running the CLI in a scratch folder with odd input. Nothing here is a guess unless it sits under "Suspicions". The earlier whole-repo scorecard is the Project Review; this note is narrower and more concrete.

Severity: High loses data or gives a wrong verdict silently, Med misleads or wastes a lot of disk or time, Low is a rough edge.

docs.title: Fixed in this pass
docs.text: # Sev What happened Fix F1 High testo clean --yes with artifacts_root: . deleted the whole project, then crashed. --temp-dir took ~ or any absolute path. #219 refuses root, home, the current folder, the config's folder, their parents, and folders holding .git / testosterone.yaml / pyproject.toml F2 High One report with time="inf", "duration": Infinity, 1e999 or an odd JSON shape ({"suites":[1]}) crashed the whole import (exit 4) and lost every other file's results #220 and #232 (importers thread): per-file catch, OverflowError handled F3 High A <testsuite> inside a root <testsuite> counted 0 tests, exit 0, so its failure was hidden #220 F4 Med testo ingest of files that all failed to parse (empty, truncated, an HTML error page) passed with 0 tests #220: exit 1 F5 Med Two stages with one name (or Unit / unit, one folder on macOS and Windows): the second reset the first's results, so a failed test vanished while the run said exit 1 #223: a config error F6 Med run.log was opened for append and never reset. Each run's log held every earlier run, and was copied whole into every history snapshot (100 MB of output, then 200 MB, ...) #223: reset when the stage starts F7 Med timeout_s: abc crashed config load with a traceback; timeout_s: 0 or -1 timed every stage out instantly; workers: 0 and version: 99 were accepted, though the JSON Schema forbids all of them #215 F8 Low A mistyped command or flag (testo frobnicate, testo run --bogus, testo split --shards 0) printed a Python traceback (standalone_mode=False let Click's UsageError escape). testo run with no --cycle said cycle '<unspecified>' not found #213: usage line + error, exit 2; #214: "pick one with --cycle" F9 Low A stage whose target_repo doesn't exist said executable not found: /nonexistent #215: names the folder F10 Low Playwright JSON with a UTF-8 BOM, a report named report[1].xml (globbed), JUnit named environment.xml outside an Allure folder, <testcase> directly under <testsuites>, and one bad xcresult duration (dropped the whole file) #218 (the rest after #220) F11 Low testo run --workers 0 or -3 was accepted. testo users add with a bad name or an existing user asked for the password twice and then said no (a bare Abort traceback without a TTY). #215, #228

docs.title: Open: proposals, not built
docs.text:
Ranked by impact. Each is bigger than a safe one-line fix or changes behaviour people may rely on, so it waits for a yes.

# Sev Problem (repro) Proposal P1 High Two runs of one cycle at once corrupt each other. Both write artifacts/<cycle>/<stage>/ and reset it on start. MODE=failed testo run --cycle c & then a passing run 1.5 s later: run A exits 1 but its record says 3 passed, 0 failed, and run.log mixes both. Two CI jobs on one runner, or testo watch plus a manual run, hit this. Short term: a lock file per cycle (artifacts/<cycle>/.lock, fcntl/msvcrt) so the second run waits or refuses with a clear message. Later: per-run folders (artifacts/<cycle>/<run-id>/), which also fixes P2. P2 High Stale stage folders count in later runs. The report collector reads every folder under artifacts/<cycle>/. A stage skipped by if:, renamed or removed keeps its old results: run 2 exits 0 / PASS while its archive row says 2 tests, 1 failed. Collect only the stages this run actually ran (pass the names from PlanResult to collect_results and aggregate_cycle_metrics). Small, but it touches the report archive, so it gets its own PR and review. P3 Med A timeout leaves grandchildren running. sh -c 'sleep 100 & wait' with timeout_s: 2: exit 124, but sleep keeps running after testo exits. Only the direct child is signalled. Start each stage in its own process group (start_new_session on POSIX, CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP on Windows) and kill the group. Must ship with P4, or Ctrl-C stops reaching the stage. P4 Med SIGTERM / Ctrl-C orphans the stage and records nothing. Killing testo mid-stage leaves the test process running, the event stream ends at stage_started, and no run row is written. With parallel stages, Ctrl-C waits about 18 s. CI cancel buttons send SIGTERM. A signal handler that terminates the running stage groups, records the run as interrupted, and exits 130 / 143. P5 Med Unknown keys are silently ignored, even by testo config validate. timeout: 1 (meant timeout_s) and env: (meant extra_env) do nothing. Warn on unknown keys with "did you mean" (difflib against the schema's keys) in validate and run; an error under testo config validate --strict. P6 Med-Low on_release can reset a key someone else now holds. A lease that missed its heartbeat (ttl 1 s, paused 1.5 s), then B takes the key, then A releases: A's on_release hook still runs on B's key. Check the lease is still ours (one heartbeat) before running on_release; skip with a warning if it isn't. P7 Low extra_env values go through str(): null becomes "None", true becomes "True", a list becomes "[1, 2]". Reject lists and mappings, map null to "" and booleans to "true" / "false". P8 Low if: misparses an env value containing == (${env:X} with X=a==b is False), and silently evaluates and / or, which it doesn't support. Interpolate after splitting on the operator, and reject expressions the grammar doesn't have. P9 Low testo split --index N prints nothing and exits 0 for an empty shard, so pytest $(testo split ...) runs every test on that shard. Exit 1 with "nothing to run on this shard" (the command already uses 1 for "nothing to split"), or document a || true pattern. P10 Low testo badge / testo flaky on a misspelt cycle say "no runs" (badge exits 0), the same as a real cycle before its first run. Add "(no cycle by that name has any runs; known: ...)" to the message. Keep exit 0, since a badge job before the first run shouldn't fail. P11 Low Engine runs store start_time as the persist (finish) time and end_time as NULL, so ordering by start is really by finish. Pass the plan's real start and end into RunRecord. P12 Low Allure attachments that are symlinks are followed, so a results folder can copy /etc/hostname into the artifacts. Local only; server uploads are plain bytes. Refuse attachments whose resolved path leaves the results folder, as report files already are. P13 Low Windows paths in Jest reports (C:\ci\repo\src\a.test.js) aren't made relative on Linux, so a CI report and a local one give different test ids. Treat drive-letter and backslash paths as absolute when relativising. P14 Low Whitespace before <?xml makes a report unreadable ("XML declaration not at start"). Strip leading whitespace before parsing. P16 Low testo ingest --server not-a-url (and split, lease) exits 3 "could not reach", as if the server were down. Check the URL has http(s):// and exit 2 for a malformed one.

docs.title: Suspicions (not reproduced)
docs.text:
• A NUL byte in a failing stage's log tail would probably break the Postgres JSONB insert, so the run row is lost (only a warning is logged).
  • _failure_result sets artifacts_dir to the allure-results folder rather than the stage folder.
  • if: and ${env:...} are resolved against os.environ, never the parent_env the API passes.

docs.title: Checked and fine
docs.text:
• Eight testo run at once on one SQLite DB: no lock errors, all eight runs recorded.
  • 3 MB of binary / invalid UTF-8 output and 100 MB of output in 2 s: no crash, memory bounded, tail decoded with replacement characters.
  • XXE and billion laughs: expat refuses external entities and stops amplification, so the file is skipped cleanly.
  • Path traversal in cycle and stage names, junit_xml patterns, Allure attachment source and Playwright attachment paths (POSIX and Windows forms): refused.
  • 50,000 test cases with emoji and 500-character names: correct counts in 26 s.
  • flaky, split, summary, report list on an empty history: clean messages.
  • Lease take race (the IntegrityError path) and heartbeat refusal after expiry.
  • Quarantine never waives a timeout or a non-1 exit code.
  • Missing or empty config, YAML syntax errors, empty stages:, unknown framework, bad args type: clean config errors, exit 2.

docs.title: Product review: scorecard and roadmap
docs.text:
Index · companion to the code-side Project Review

The Project Review asked "is the code good?" and ended at 10. This note asks a different question: would a team pick Testosterone over what they already use, and would they keep using it? It looks at the product, not the code: positioning against the tools people actually adopt, the first ten minutes, the daily "why is CI red" workflow, the UI's design, accessibility and copy.

How the first pass was checked (2026-10-24, main at 9104054):

  • Competitors: Allure Report and Allure TestOps, ReportPortal, Currents, Trunk Flaky Tests, Datadog Test Optimization, Testmo and TestDino, from their own docs and comparison pages. Prices change often and some comparison pages are written by a competitor, so treat the figures as rough.
  • The demo UI: the same static site that the Pages demo publishes, built locally from self-test and sample-all-frameworks runs, plus the README screenshots of the failing fake-api runs. Every page was opened at 1280 px and 390 px.
  • Accessibility: an automated axe-core 4.10 scan (WCAG 2 A/AA and best practice) of every page, keyboard tabbing through the shell, and a touch-target and horizontal-overflow check at 390 px. Automated scans catch about a third of real issues; no screen reader was used.
  • Copy: the CLI's --help, the README, and the UI's headings, empty states and error messages.
  • Prior work: the 2026-10-22 gaps review (ingest mode, team server, positioning, lean install, alerts, quarantine, Playwright, JSON Schema). All of those have shipped since, so this review starts where that one ended.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Overall: 8.5 / 10 as a product (was 7.5), and 9 or more in every area except trust. Third pass, 2026-10-25, main at ed57b9d, after the Product to Ten work in #176 to #184. Every item in What a 10 needs that didn't wait on Taltal has shipped: recorded cycles have pages, "new" means new since the target branch, the dashboard leads with what needs attention, pytest --testo records a local run with no CI step, and the test page has attachments, traces, flakiness over time and a remembered cause.

What keeps the areas from 10 is small and listed under Third pass findings: a cycle's own run history is hard to see (P15), the duration chart has no scale (D8), and three copy nits. What keeps the product from 10 overall is trust (one maintainer, nothing launched), which no pull request fixes.

How it was checked: a live API and UI built from main, with six ingested JUnit runs of a web cycle (a flaky test, a shared ConnectionRefusedError, a test that keeps getting slower), a Playwright JSON import with a screenshot, a video and a trace, and a pytest --testo session on a branch. Every page opened at 1280 px, 390 px and 640 × 450 (200 % zoom); axe-core (WCAG 2 A/AA and best practice) on every page; triage marked and inherited in the browser. No screen reader, no users.

Area To reach 10 Realistic Time to first value P10 (ingest cycles get pages), a first-run empty state in testo ui with the testo ingest command, and a pytest plugin (pytest -p testo or pytest --testo) that records every local run with no CI step Yes Core workflow P11 to P14: "new since main" on the run page, branch and commit in its header, Compare prefilled with the run and its baseline, and a copyable "rerun these" command per runner (pytest node ids, --grep for Playwright) Yes Visual design D7: a dashboard that answers "what needs me?" docs.text:
# Severity Finding Fix P15 Medium A cycle's own run history is hard to see. Runs lists every cycle together with no filter, and a cycle's page shows its tests, flaky card and stages but not its runs or how often it has passed lately A cycle filter on Runs (/runs?cycle=web) and a "Recent runs" card on the cycle page with the pass rate over those runs, linking to the filtered list D8 Low The test page's duration chart has no scale: equal durations draw full-height bars, so a steady 300 ms test looks as busy as one swinging from 1 to 9 s Label the chart's top value and draw bars from zero against it C11 Low Slowdowns read "+1.1 s (+95.5%)" on the cycle page and "+1.1 s (+96%)" on the dashboard One formatter for both (formatPercent) C12 Low "0 of 3 cycles passed their latest run; 3 cycles are red." "All 3 cycles are red." when none passed C13 Low Runs says "Every archived cycle run, newest first." Second-pass findings P10 to P14, D7, A8, A9, C8 and C10 are fixed (#176 to #181). Third-pass findings P15, D8 and C11 to C13 are fixed since (see Product to Ten).

docs.title: Second pass verdict (2026-10-25)
docs.text:
Overall: 7.5 / 10 as a product (was 6.5). Second pass, 2026-10-25, main at ad4dc9f, after the roadmap work in #166 to #174 (Product Roadmap Work). The red build now lands: the run page leads with its failing tests, groups shared causes, says how long each has failed and links to a page per test, and PR comments compare with the target branch. The first look is three commands (pip install, testo ingest, testo ui) or no install at all on the try-it page.

It is 7.5 rather than the 8 the first pass predicted because of one new finding: a cycle that only exists through testo ingest has no cycle page (P10). GET /api/v1/cycles/{name} reads testosterone.yaml, so the cycle every ingest user creates is missing from Cycles and its page answers "not found", which hides the test search, the slowest tests and the flaky card from exactly the users the first look was rebuilt for. Fixing it is the single biggest step to 8.

How it was checked: the static demo rebuilt from self-test, sample-all-frameworks and three ingested JUnit runs of a web cycle; every page opened at 1280 px and 390 px; axe-core (WCAG 2 A/AA and best practice) on every page; keyboard tabbing through the shell; touch targets and overflow at 390 px; the API called directly for the ingest-only cycle. No screen reader, no users.

docs.text:
# Severity Finding Fix P10 High Ingest-only cycles have no page. GET /api/v1/cycles/web answers 404 ("Unknown cycle") for a cycle created by testo ingest, while /analytics/tests?cycle=web has its tests. Cycles doesn't list it and the static export skips it List cycles from run history as well as config; a history-only cycle gets a read-only page (no Run panel) with its tests, flaky card and runs P11 Medium "New" on the run page is relative to the previous run on any branch. load_run_failures walks the cycle's earlier runs regardless of branch, so on a busy repo "New" and "Failing for N runs" mix branches. #170 fixed this for the PR comment only Use the same baseline as the PR comment (pick_baseline): earlier runs on the run's target or default branch, falling back to all runs; say which in the card P12 Low The run page doesn't show the branch, commit or PR it ran for, though the run records them A line under the title: branch, short commit (linked when repository is set) P13 Low Compare opens with nothing selected, and same-minute runs read the same ("web · Oct 25 03:37" twice; D3 from the first pass) Prefill the latest run and its baseline; label runs with seconds or a run number and branch P14 Low No "rerun what failed" A copy button on the failing-tests card with the runner's command for those tests D7 Medium The dashboard is still data-model first (see Design and UX above); D6's icon tiles are unchanged Lead with what needs attention; status-coloured or no icons A8 Minor axe "region" on every page: the skip link sits before the sidebar, outside every landmark (it is the only content that does) Put it inside a landmark (the header, or a nav labelled "Skip links") A9 Minor Under the 24 px minimum target (WCAG 2.2 2.5.8): the demo notice's close button (26 × 26 px), inline "compare" and run links 15–18 px high in lists 44 px close button; give list rows a taller hit area C10 Low "Generate AI Summary", "Trend: regressed" / "Trend: flat", "Irregular tier mix", "Non-ideal tier ordering", health as 20.00% "Generate AI summary", "Down from 40%" / "No change", "Mostly unit tests", whole-number percentages

First-pass findings P1 to P9, D1, D2, D4, D5, A1 to A7, C1 to C7 and C9 are fixed (#166 to #174). D3 and D6 are carried into P13 and D7, and C8 is still open.

Since the second pass, everything in What a 10 needs that doesn't wait on Taltal has shipped: #176 to #184, plus the comparison page (#185).

docs.title: First pass verdict (2026-10-24)
docs.text:
Overall: 6.5 / 10 as a product (the code scores 10). The engineering is ahead of the product. Every capability a team needs is there: ingest from any runner, a shared server, flaky detection and quarantine, PR comments and annotations, Slack and Teams alerts, run-to-run diffs, AI summaries. But the two moments that decide adoption are weaker than the features behind them:

  1. The first look. A pip install user has no UI. testo-api serves one only when TESTO_UI_DIR points at a frontend/dist you built yourself from a checkout with npm, and Getting Started says the web UI "runs from a checkout of the repository". So the laptop story ends in the terminal, and the screenshots in the README show something a new user can't get without cloning the repo or running the Docker team server.
  2. The red build. The question the README promises to answer is "what broke?". The run page doesn't answer it: it shows a run ID, Type: cycle, Return code 1, report links, a test pyramid that says Healthy pyramid on a failed run, and per-stage health. It never lists the failing tests, their error messages or how long they've been failing. You get there through Compare, the Allure report or the AI summary. And the PR comment compares with "the previous run of the cycle", which on a busy team is somebody else's branch, so "what changed" turns into noise.

Fix those two and the product score moves to about 8 without a new feature. After that, the gap to the paid tools is the per-test view (history, flake rate, duration trend, owner) and grouping failures by cause.

docs.title: First pass scorecard
docs.text: Area Score In one line Positioning and value proposition 7.5 The README and PyPI summary now lead with the outcome ("what broke, what's flaky and what got slower"), and "a pip install that keeps the history" is a real gap between Allure (one run) and ReportPortal (a server to run). The CLI's own tagline still says "unified quality orchestration CLI", and the name still costs search and workplace adoption (open decision from the gaps review) Time to first value 6 testo ingest is one CI step with no config, which is excellent. Seeing it in a UI needs a checkout and npm, or Docker. No hosted "try it with your JUnit file" either Core workflow: "why is CI red?" 5.5 The run page has no failing-test list; the baseline is the previous run, not the main branch; there is no page for one test across runs; failures aren't grouped by message Feature depth against competitors 7.5 Ahead of every free tool on history, diffs and flaky quarantine; behind Trunk and Datadog on per-test analytics, ownership and tickets; behind Currents on live per-test streaming and traces Visual design and UX 7 Clean, consistent, responsive. Hierarchy follows the data model (summary, reports, pyramid, stages) instead of the user's question; prime space goes to IDs, a "Need help?" card and status chips; some numbers are noise (a 0.3 % change shown as a red Regression) Accessibility 7 Few automated issues and a real main landmark, labelled controls and aria-expanded on most toggles. One page overflows at phone width, primary buttons fall just short of 4.5:1, small touch targets, no skip link, heading levels skip UX copy 6.5 The demo notice and empty states are friendly. Errors say "Failed to load X." with no cause or next step; engineer words (Return code, Type: cycle, Trend: unknown, state unknown) reach the UI; title case, sentence case and two kinds of ellipsis are mixed; --help shows literal RST backticks Trust and adoption signals 5 PyPI, Docker images, a docs site, a live demo, CI badges and a contributor. Still one maintainer, no "used by", no launch post (drafts exist, nothing posted)

docs.title: Competitive position
docs.text:
What it is Where Testosterone wins Where it loses Allure Report Free HTML report for one run (with an optional history folder) Real history and diffs across runs, a shared server, flaky detection; Testosterone can still produce Allure reports Allure's per-test page (steps, attachments, retries) is far richer than anything in Testosterone's own UI Allure TestOps Paid test management with launches and dashboards Free, small, pip install, no test-case management to adopt Test cases, manual testing, custom dashboards, role-based views, SSO ReportPortal Open-source server with ML failure clustering; SaaS is enterprise-priced One pip install or one docker compose up instead of a multi-service deployment Auto-analysis that sorts failures into product bug, test bug or system issue, and remembers the decision; per-test history Currents Cloud dashboard for Playwright and Cypress, usage-priced (from about $49/month) Any runner, self-hosted, free Live streaming per test, traces and videos in the browser, CI orchestration and load balancing Trunk Flaky Tests Hosted flaky detection and quarantine (free tier, then per committer) Self-hosted, free, also runs the tests and does diffs Per-test pages, automatic quarantine, Jira and Linear tickets, "PRs rescued" metrics, test collections Datadog Test Optimization Test analytics inside Datadog (per committer) No Datadog account, no per-seat bill Flaky management at scale, test impact analysis, correlation with traces and deploys

The position to own: the free, self-hosted Trunk-and-Currents for teams that can't or won't send test data to a SaaS. History, diffs, flaky quarantine and PR feedback for any runner, in one pip install or one container. It is already true on paper. The roadmap below makes it true in the first ten minutes and on the red-build page.

docs.title: First pass findings
docs.text: Severity is product impact: High decides whether someone adopts or keeps the tool, Medium costs trust or time every day, Low is polish.

docs.title: Product and workflow
docs.text: # Severity Finding Suggested fix Size P1 High The run page doesn't show what failed. RunDetailPage has Summary, Report Links, Test Pyramid, Stage Health, Artifacts and the AI summary, but no list of failing tests or their messages Put a "Failing tests" card first on any failed run: test name, stage, first line of the message, "failing since" and a flaky badge, each opening the test's page (P4) M P2 High No UI for pip install users. The wheel doesn't contain the built frontend; TESTO_UI_DIR must point at a local npm run build Build the frontend in the release workflow, ship it in the wheel and add testo ui (open the browser on the local history). Already on the after-publish ideas list M P3 High "What changed" compares with the previous run, not with main. run_summary_markdown and the dashboard take the cycle's previous run as the baseline. With several PRs running, that's another branch Record branch and commit on every run (ingest already sends them), and default the baseline to the latest run of the same cycle on the default branch, falling back to the previous run M P4 Medium No page for one test. You can't open a test and see its pass/fail history, flake rate, duration trend and last failure message /tests/:cycle/:id page plus a test search box. It's the page every competitor builds first, and the flaky card and P1 can link to it M P5 Medium Failures aren't grouped. Ten tests failing with the same ConnectionRefusedError show as ten separate failures Group failing tests by a normalised first line of the message ("3 failures: connection refused") on the run page and in the PR comment S P6 Medium Performance deltas have no noise floor. A +10 ms (+0.3 %) change in test time is a red Regression chip, so the Performance rollup is almost never clean Treat changes under a threshold (for example 5 % and 100 ms) as unchanged, and say so in the Delta Comparison Policy S P7 Medium No slowest-tests view. "What got slower" is in the tagline, but only whole-run and per-stage durations are shown A "Slowest tests" and "Got slower" list on the cycle page, from durations already recorded S P8 Low Flaky tests stop at the list. No owner (most repos already have a CODEOWNERS file), no "open an issue" link Show the owner from CODEOWNERS and a prefilled GitHub issue link on each flaky test S P9 Low No way to try it without installing. The demo shows our data only Later: a drop-a-JUnit-file page on the demo that renders it in the browser (no upload) L

docs.title: Design
docs.text: # Severity Finding Suggested fix D1 Medium The run page's top half is a run UUID, Type, Return code, wall time in ms and report links: data a human rarely needs first. The status, the failing tests and "what changed" should be above the fold Order: status and one-line verdict ("5 failed, 3 new since main"), failing tests, what changed, then stages, pyramid and reports. Move the UUID into a copy button D2 Medium Mixed signals: a failed run shows Healthy pyramid in green, and the header shows a green All systems go (it means the API's database is up) next to a red run Rename the status dot to "API connected" (or show it only when something is wrong); call the pyramid "Test mix" and drop the health colour D3 Medium Compare labels both runs "fake-api · Oct 22 04:00" when they ran in the same minute; the only difference is an 8-character hash Show seconds or a run number (#41 vs #42) and the branch D4 Low Durations switch between 6429 ms and 6.43 s on neighbouring pages One formatter: seconds above 1 s everywhere D5 Low The "Need help? docs.title: What this review does not cover
docs.text: No user interviews or usage data exist yet, so every finding is an expert review, not evidence of what users do. The first real signal will come from the launch: watch which page people land on, which install path they take, and which issues they open, then revisit this note.

docs.title: Project review: scorecard and verdict
docs.text:
Index

Six passes over the whole repo with the tech-debt, code-review, security-review and architecture checklists (the first pass also used testing-strategy). The sixth pass is main plus throwaway stage containers (TESTO_RUNNER=container), after #163 fixed S10 and S11, 2026-10-24. The fifth pass was main after #159 to #161, the fourth was 06e636c, the third 63ca88f, the second 3aeb3b3 and the first f1e3521, all the same day; their findings are kept below with their status. Open items that should outlive this note move to the Technical Debt Tracker.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Overall: 10 / 10 (was 9.5; the first pass was 8). The fifth pass set the bar for a 10 as "safe to expose to people you don't trust", and named three things missing. All three are now in, each a switch that is off by default, so one developer or a small team gets exactly the old behaviour:

  • Sign-in throttling (S11, #163): with accounts, repeated wrong passwords for a name or from an address get 429.
  • Reports on their own origin (S10, #163): TESTO_REPORTS_ORIGIN serves report pages from a second hostname with a cookie that can only read reports.
  • Throwaway stage containers: TESTO_RUNNER=container sends each stage to a separate runner service that starts it in a fresh container: no capabilities, no privilege escalation, a process limit, fixed image and mounts, an allow-list of commands, and only the stage's own variables. The API never gets the Docker socket, and a test can no longer read the server's token or database URL. See Throwaway Stage Containers.

A 10 here is not "nothing left": S12 (stages share the artifacts volume, Low) and the runner service's Docker socket are documented trade-offs, one server process is still the supported setup, and TypeScript 7 waits on typescript-eslint. None of them is a defect in what the project claims to do.

docs.title: Scorecard
docs.text: Area Score Was In one line Architecture 10 9.5 One engine, one service entry point, plugins, a read-side history/. Where a stage runs is a backend behind one launch() (the slot the executor's docstring had reserved), so host and container share the log, timeout, JUnit and quarantine code; every team feature is a switch with an ADR Code quality 9.5 9 ruff, ruff format, mypy and ESLint clean, vulture empty, no TODOs, no module over 500 lines (largest: cycle_execution_manager.py, 493) Tests 9.5 9 987 fast tests at 86% coverage on Python 3.11 to 3.13; both settings of each switch tested. The runner tests run the real service with a stand-in docker (stream, env boundary, timeout, a vanished API), and the container path was also run against a real Docker daemon Security 10 9.5 Accounts, throttled sign-in, a separate report origin and sandboxed stages, all opt-in. Left: S12 (Low, documented) and the runner service's socket, which is the documented price of keeping it out of the API Docs 9.5 9 Linted vault, an ADR per team feature, a Team Server section per switch with its variables, a security model that says what each switch does and doesn't protect CI / DX 9.5 9 Python matrix, ESLint, OpenAPI and schema drift checks, image scan and start check for all three images (the runner service is new), team server smoke, tolerant publish Tech debt 9.5 9 Nothing from earlier passes is open but TypeScript 7 (blocked upstream). The cost of the switches is two tested modes each

docs.title: What was checked (sixth pass)
docs.text: Check Result ruff check ., ruff format --check ., mypy, OpenAPI drift Clean (mypy: the review machine's known stale-package errors only) pytest -m "tier_fast and not quarantined" 987 passed, 86% coverage; backends/container.py and runner_service.py 84% (the rest is the main() loop and Docker error paths) Runner service by hand, real Docker The stage container has CapEff 0, runs as 10001, sees the stage's variables and not TESTO_API_TOKEN; results land on the shared volume; a timeout gives 124 and removes the container; closing the API's connection removes it within a second; the service image starts and reaches the socket through group_add Request checks Command by name from the allow-list, directory inside a mount, no .., valid variable names, DOCKER_*/PATH/HOME dropped, values passed as -e NAME (not on the command line), --flag=value so nothing in the request reads as a Docker flag; image and mounts never come from the request Default path TESTO_RUNNER unset: the executor calls subprocess.Popen with the same arguments as before; the existing executor tests pass unchanged

docs.title: Sixth-pass findings
docs.text: # Severity Finding Fix Status S12 Low Stage containers share the artifacts volume. Every stage mounts the whole testo_artifacts volume read-write, so a malicious test in one run could read or change another run's artifacts. It can't reach the server's token, database or report history Mount a per-run subpath (Docker 26+ volume-subpath) Accepted, documented in the ADR

docs.text: Check Result ruff check ., ruff format --check ., mypy, ESLint, tsc Clean (mypy: the review machine's 2 known stale-package errors only) pytest -m "tier_fast and not quarantined" 952 passed, 86% coverage; new modules 90% or more (run_queue.py 94, security.py 94, accounts.py 90, auth.py 92) #159 _worker_loop catches BaseException per job, _ensure_workers drops dead threads; reproduced the old failure, now a test #160 run queue A row is deleted (atomically) as its run starts, so an interrupted run is never repeated and two processes never both run a row; recovered runs keep their execution id; a DB error on enqueue frees the cycle #161 accounts Salted scrypt, dummy hash for unknown names, cookie signed with the token and tied to a session version, role checked on every write, reads always protected, every write and sign-in audited, /login still refuses foreign origins, token mode byte-for-byte the old path Open pull requests Only #106 (TypeScript 7, blocked by typescript-eslint)

docs.title: Fifth-pass findings
docs.text: # Severity Finding Fix Status S10 Low Report pages share the API's origin. S9 sandboxed attachments, but the Allure report pages under /history run script on the server's origin. With accounts, a viewer opening a report that an XSS in the report generator let through would act with the viewer's role. Needs a bug in Allure's own escaping, and a viewer can't write anyway Serve /history from a separate origin (TESTO_REPORTS_ORIGIN) if the server is exposed to people you don't trust Fixed (#163) S11 Low No sign-in lockout. Each failed attempt costs an scrypt hash and is audited, but nothing slows a password guesser down Rate-limit /api/v1/auth/login at the reverse proxy (documented in the security model), or add a per-name backoff Fixed (#163)

docs.title: What was checked (fourth pass, 06e636c)
docs.text: Check Result ruff check . and ruff format --check . Clean pytest -m "tier_fast and not quarantined" 919 passed, 0 failed, 86% coverage, on the review machine too vulture --min-confidence 80, TODO/FIXME Nothing #156 worker pool FIFO queue, one cycle queued or running at a time, queued status in the API models and the UI, workers started lazily. A job that raises BaseException kills its worker (A4, checked by running one) #156 parallel stages Events and the renderer stay on the calling thread, results keep config order, fail_fast starts nothing new after a failure, duplicate stage names refused when parallel, live output buffered per stage Open pull requests Only #106 (TypeScript 7, blocked by typescript-eslint)

docs.title: Fourth-pass findings
docs.text: # Severity Finding Fix Status A4 Low A worker that hits SystemExit is never replaced. _run_execution catches Exception, so a SystemExit or KeyboardInterrupt raised during a run (a reporter plugin calling sys.exit(), say) ends _worker_loop's thread. The run itself is marked failed, but _ensure_workers counts dead threads, so the pool shrinks for good; with the default of 2, two such runs leave every later run queued forever Catch BaseException per job in _worker_loop (log it and keep looping), or drop dead threads in _ensure_workers, plus a test Fixed (#159) D10 Code Three modules over 500 lines, and two grew this round: cycle_execution_manager.py (539 to 581) and config/loader.py (537 to 560) Split the worker pool and the SSE helpers out of the manager, and the cycle parsing out of the loader, the next time each changes Fixed (#159)

A script in it runs with the viewer's session and passes the Origin check, so it can start runs. With one shared token, the uploader already has that power, so nothing is gained today. There are also no X-Content-Type-Options or frame-ancestors headers Send Content-Security-Policy: sandbox and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on /history responses, and frame-ancestors 'self' everywhere. Serving reports from a separate origin only matters once there are per-user accounts Fixed (#155) T6 Test Two tests still assume a contributor's machine: the packaging contract fails when build isn't installed, and the rootdir test picks a pytest on PATH that belongs to another interpreter (without allure-pytest). T3 fixed the case where no pytest is found, but not this one Skip the build check when the module is missing, and run sys.executable -m pytest in the rootdir test Fixed (#155)

docs.text:
All Low, most severe first. None was a blocker.

# Severity Finding Fix Status S6 Low Protected reads are only on in the compose file. The testo-server image itself does not set TESTO_PROTECT_READS, so docker run -e TESTO_API_TOKEN=... testo-server serves runs, logs and reports to anyone who can reach it Set TESTO_PROTECT_READS=1 in Dockerfile.testo-server so the image is safe by default, as the compose file already is Fixed (#150) S7 Low Sessions are stateless. The cookie is an HMAC of the token, so sign-out only clears the browser's copy; a copied cookie works until the token changes, for up to 30 days Acceptable with one shared token; document "rotate the token to sign everyone out", or add a server-side session list if per-user accounts arrive Documented (#150) S8 Info No rate limit on /login. A guessed token is the only way in, and the guides tell people to use openssl rand -hex 32, so online guessing is not practical Nothing now; a reverse proxy can rate-limit if needed Accepted S5 Low AI base_url is free-form (open from the first pass). A write token can point the provider at any URL, and the key goes there One sentence in the security model Documented (#150) T5 Test Lowest-covered modules: reporting/allure.py 32%, reporting/server.py 37%, frameworks/behave_adapter.py 45%, reporting/behavex_allure.py 48%, cli/commands/watch.py 48% Tests for the Allure CLI fallbacks and the Behave adapter's argument building Fixed (#157) D8 Dependency Nine Dependabot pull requests (#132 to #140) are open, including actions/setup-python 7 and @testing-library/jest-dom 7 (a major bump), and #105 is superseded by the merged Vite 8 upgrade Review and merge the green ones; close #105 Done (#151 and the merged Dependabot PRs; #106 blocked upstream) D9 Process Contributor PR #124 has waited since 2026-10-21 for a merge from main Nudge or take it over with credit Done (#152; #124 shows merged)

An earlier run showed 2 errors in repository/models.py; that came from stale packages in the review machine's global environment, not from the code python scripts/docs_vault.py lint ok pytest -m "tier_fast and not quarantined" 813 passed, 4 failed, 79.4% coverage. All 4 failures were the review machine: no build module, the bdd extra failed to install, and one test that expects pytest next to sys.executable npm audit (frontend) 0 in production dependencies; 6 in dev tooling (Vitest, esbuild, tinypool) pip-audit Nothing in the project's own dependencies vulture --min-confidence 80 2 unused variables; manual check found unused functions in reporting/report_generator.py (see D1)

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The design matches ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architecture Overview: config/loader.py → config/resolver.py → engine/orchestrator.run_plan() → engine/executor.run_stage(), with both the CLI and the API going through services/cycle_run.CycleRunService (the only caller of run_plan). Ingest reuses the same service through equipment: junit, so uploaded results get the same history, Compare, flaky detection and reporters as real runs. That is the strongest part of the project: features added in October (ingest, team server, quarantine, alerts, Playwright JSON) slotted in without a second path.

Strengths

  • Framework adapters behind a small protocol (frameworks/base.py), and third-party runners and reporters through entry points (plugins.py), so new runners need no core change.
  • Storage behind persistence/ and repository/, reads behind history/, SQLite by default and Postgres for the team server.
  • Exit codes single-sourced in engine/exit_codes.py and locked by contract tests.
  • The frontend's API types are generated from OpenAPI and CI fails when they drift.

Risks to watch

  • A1. Thread-per-run API. Fixed: executions now queue for a pool of TESTO_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS workers (default 2); see Scale Runs and Stages - 2026-10-24. State is still in memory. Was: testo_api/cycle_execution_manager.py starts a daemon thread per execution and keeps state in memory. One run per cycle is enforced, which is right, but there is no global cap on concurrent runs and a restart loses live state (orphans are cleaned up on startup). Fine for a local tool and a small team server; a queue would be the next step if the server grows.
  • A2. Sequential stages. Fixed: a cycle can opt in with max_parallel_stages: N (same note).
  • A3. Version hard-coded twice. Fixed (#141). testo_api/main.py sets version="1.1.1" by hand next to pyproject.toml. Read it from importlib.metadata so a release can't leave the API reporting an old version.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
The model in ARCHITECTURE.md § Security model is sound and the code follows it: loopback by default, foreign-origin writes refused even without a token (which stops simple cross-site POSTs and DNS rebinding), hmac.compare_digest for the token, upload size limits, sanitised upload filenames, Playwright attachments confined to the report root, secret redaction before AI calls, and the team server's compose file refuses to start without TESTO_API_TOKEN. No workflow uses pull_request_target, and 10 of 13 set explicit permissions: (see S4).

Findings, most severe first

# Severity Finding Fix Status S1 Medium Open reads take an arbitrary file path. GET /api/v1/cycles, GET /api/v1/cycles/{cycle} and GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/pyramid accept ?config_path= and load it. Reads need no token even when TESTO_API_TOKEN is set, so anyone who can reach a team server can probe whether any file exists and see fragments of non-YAML files in the error message (checked: config_path=/root/.bashrc returns a line of the file in the YAML parse error) Drop config_path from GET routes, or restrict it to files under the configured project root, and return a generic error message Fixed (#141) S2 Medium Public bind without a token only warns. testo-api on a non-loopback host with no TESTO_API_TOKEN logs a warning and starts, and the testo-server image binds 0.0.0.0. A plain docker run -p 8000:8000 testo-server exposes "start a run", which runs commands, to the network Refuse to start in that case unless an explicit TESTO_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=1 is set Fixed (#141) S3 Low Reads and /history are open on the team server. Run logs and report files can carry secrets printed by tests. Documented in the Team Server guide, but there is no switch to protect them Add an opt-in TESTO_API_READ_TOKEN (or require the token for reads when set) Fixed (#147) S4 Low Floating action refs and default token scope. aquasecurity/trivy-action@master and anthropics/claude-code-base-action@beta run in the Docker publish and changelog-on-main workflows, and commitlint.yml, pr-heavy.yml and release-gate.yml have no permissions: block, so they get the repository's default token scope. A compromised upstream branch would run with those jobs' secrets Pin the two actions to a release tag or commit SHA (Dependabot already watches github-actions) and add permissions: contents: read to the three workflows Fixed (#141) S5 Low AI base_url is free-form. With a write token, the AI settings page can point the provider at any URL and the server will send the key there. Acceptable for a self-hosted tool; worth a sentence in the security model Document it, optionally allow-list schemes and hosts Documented (#150)

XML from uploads is parsed with the standard library's ElementTree, which on Python 3.11+ does not resolve external entities and has expat's entity-expansion limits, and uploads are size-capped, so XXE and billion-laughs are not a concern.

docs.title: Code quality and tech debt
docs.text:
Prioritised with the tech-debt formula, priority = (impact + risk) × (6 − effort), each scored 1 to 5.

# Item Type Impact Risk Effort Priority Status S1 config_path on open GET routes Security 2 4 1 30 Fixed (#141) S2 Public bind without token is fail-open Security 2 4 1 30 Fixed (#141) D2 Large unreleased backlog: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] holds ingest, the team server, Playwright JSON, quarantine, alerts, the config schema, the plugin API and a breaking extras change. PyPI users are on 1.1.1 Release 4 3 2 28 Released as v1.2.0, on PyPI D1 Streamlit-era dead code in reporting/report_generator.py: sync_all_reports_to_static, start_report_server, start_static_server, collect_behavex_native_report and url_for have no caller in testo_core/ or testo_api/, and six comments still mention Streamlit, which was removed in v1.1 Code 3 2 1 25 Fixed (#141) D3 No Python version matrix: classifiers claim 3.12 and 3.13, CI runs only 3.11 Infrastructure 2 3 1 25 Fixed (#141) T1 Thin coverage where users plug in: TestBeats reporter 18%, cli/commands/config.py 19%, ReportPortal reporter 26%, Anthropic provider 30%, cli/commands/report.py 39% Test 3 3 3 18 Fixed (#143) D4 No Python lock or constraints file, only lower bounds, so CI resolves the newest dependencies on every run and an upstream release can turn main red with no change here. Normal for a library; checked that today's latest versions pass mypy and the suite on 3.12 and 3.13 Dependency 1 2 2 12 Accepted D5 Frontend dependency debt: Dependabot PRs for Vite 8 (#105) and TypeScript 7 (#106) break the build; dev tooling has 6 npm audit advisories Dependency 2 2 3 12 Vite 8 done (#146); TypeScript 7 blocked upstream D6 testo_core/mascot/ (422 lines, 0% coverage) ships inside the core package for a UI animation Code 1 1 2 8 Fixed (#148) D7 No frontend linter (ESLint or Biome); tsc is the only static check Infrastructure 1 2 2 12 Fixed (#144)

Good habits worth keeping: no TODO or FIXME markers in the Python packages, every broad except Exception has a comment saying why, 14 type: ignores across ~20k lines, and functions are small with a few exceptions (config/loader.py, reporting/report_generator.py, cli/commands/report.py and testo_api/cycle_execution_manager.py are each 500+ lines).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
The suite is a pyramid in the right shape: 102 unit files, 19 contract files (exit codes, CI tiers, packaging, OpenAPI), 7 integration and 3 end-to-end, with tiers and a quarantine marker. The fast tier runs in about 16 seconds, which keeps it on every pull request, and coverage is 79% against a 65% gate. The project also tests itself through its own GitHub Action and the fake-api demo, which is a strong signal.

Gaps

  • T1 above: reporters and CLI report commands are where outside users integrate, and they are the least covered.
  • T2. Fixed (#145). The frontend has 17 test files for ~8k lines of TypeScript. The Compare and Run Detail pages carry the product's main story and deserve component tests for their empty, error and loading states.
  • T3. Fixed (#141). A few tests assume the machine: test_target_inside_another_pytest_project_keeps_its_own_rootdir expects pytest next to sys.executable, and the packaging contract needs build. Skip them with a clear reason when the tool is missing, so a contributor's first local run is green.
  • T4. Fixed (#141). With no 3.12/3.13 job (D3), the version claims in pyproject.toml are untested.

docs.title: Docs and developer experience
docs.text:
The vault is the project's best interview asset: a linted entry point, ADRs per decision, an architecture document with a security model and known limits, a getting-started guide that CI runs end to end, and a docs site. CONTRIBUTING.md, issue and PR templates, SECURITY.md, a code of conduct and CITATION.cff are all present.

Small gaps: actionlint_py-1.7.12.25.tar.gz was committed (removed in #141) at the repo root and looks like a stray download, and the README is 333 lines, so a newcomer has to scroll past a lot before the first command.

docs.title: What's left
docs.text:
1. Hardening the container runner further. Per-run artifact subpaths (S12), and a Kubernetes or rootless backend behind the same three endpoints for teams that don't want a Docker socket anywhere.
  2. When upstream allows. TypeScript 7 once typescript-eslint supports it.
  3. If the team server outgrows one process. A shared one-run-per-cycle guard and concurrency cap across processes; the durable queue already claims rows safely.
