docs.title: Command Reference
docs.text:
Entry point: testo (pyproject.toml → testo_core.cli.app:main).

Parent index: Index. Architecture: Architecture Overview. Run lifecycle: QA Strategies.

testo --help

Help is grouped into panels: Run and report, Config, Diagnostics, Maintenance, About.

Extras: pip install testo-core is the CLI with pytest, Playwright, command and junit stages. Add [bdd] for behave and behavex stages (Behave, BehaveX and Allure-Behave), [api] for the REST API and UI backend, [db] for Postgres or MySQL, [metrics] for InfluxDB, [otel] for OpenTelemetry export. A behave stage without the extra fails with exit 3 and executable not found: behave (... pip install 'testo-core[bdd]').

docs.title: testo run
docs.text:
Execute one cycle or all cycles from testosterone.yaml.

testo run --cycle sample-pytests
testo run --cycle sample-pytests --ci
testo run --cycle sample-pytests --stream
testo run --cycle sample-pytests --workers 8 --force

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Flag Short Description --cycle Cycle name from cycles:; use all for every cycle (sorted), each trigger evaluated separately --plan -p Deprecated alias for --cycle (hidden) --config -c Path to testosterone.yaml (default: discovery) --stream Tail each stage stdout live (vs post-mortem Rich panel) --ci NDJSON events on stdout instead of Rich UI --no-persist Skip optional run-history DB writes --no-report-db Skip archiving cycle artifacts to report DB after run --async-report-db Archive in background thread with join timeout; ignored when --ci is set --workers -w Override parallel workers (e.g. BehaveX); 1 or more --force -f Run even when trigger would skip the cycle --coverage Code coverage report the tests write (repeatable): Cobertura or JaCoCo XML, LCOV, or a Go cover profile. Read when the stages finish; its line coverage is stored with the run and shown on the run page, the PR comment and the digest. A missing file only logs a warning. Not with --cycle all

[!warning] Roadmap flags — not implemented yet --tag, --fail-fast, --dry-run and --reporter were previously listed here but are not present in testo_core/cli/commands/run.py. The API layer already accepts fail_fast and reporter_override on POST /api/v1/cycles/{cycle}/executions (surfaced in the React Run panel); the CLI flags remain roadmap items. (Doc corrected 2026-07-04 during the Phase 5 UI redesign.)

docs.title: Expected terminal output
docs.text:
Interactive (default): Rich panels for plan start, each stage, and finish. On success:

Run finished successfully.

On failure:

Run exited with code 1.

--ci: One NDJSON object per line (plan_started, stage_started, stage_finished, plan_finished, etc.), no Rich styling.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: See Architecture Overview § Exit code contract. testo run returns the engine exit code directly.

docs.title: testo ingest
docs.text:
Record test results that another step already wrote (any runner, any language) as a run of a cycle. Nothing is executed: the files are parsed into the same run history as testo run, so Compare, trends, testo flaky, reporters and the PR comment work on them.

testo ingest 'reports/**/*.xml' --cycle web-unit          # record locally
testo ingest junit.xml --cycle api --tier integration --ci
testo ingest test-results/results.json --cycle web-e2e --stage e2e --tier e2e   # Playwright JSON
testo ingest allure-results --cycle api                    # a folder: the files in it
testo ingest 'reports/*.xml' --cycle web-unit \
  --server https://testo.example.com --token "$TESTO_API_TOKEN"   # team server
Flag Default Meaning REPORTS... required Files, folders (their files) or quoted globs, relative to --repo (absolute paths must be inside it). Each file is recognised by its content; see the table below --cycle required Cycle name the run is recorded under: letters, digits, ., _, -. Reuse it so runs build a history --stage junit Stage name the tests are grouped under --tier unit Test-pyramid tier: unit, integration, e2e --repo . Directory the report paths are relative to --config / -c discovered testosterone.yaml for reporters: and paths; not required --ci off NDJSON events on stdout, as testo run --ci (with --server: one ingest_uploaded event) --no-persist off Parse only, record nothing --server $TESTO_SERVER_URL Upload to a team server instead of recording locally --token $TESTO_API_TOKEN The server's API token --coverage none Code coverage report to store with the run (repeatable, relative to --repo), as testo run --coverage. Checked first: no match or an unknown format is exit 2. With --server only the totals are sent (the server recomputes the percentage)

Files it reads, with the command that writes each one (no extra package needed except where noted):

Runner Write results with Read as pytest pytest --junitxml=junit.xml (or pytest --testo) JUnit XML Jest npx jest --json --outputFile=jest.json (or equipment: jest) Jest JSON: describe blocks, retried tests flagged flaky, test files that failed to load. Prefer it to jest-junit, which drops a test file that fails to compile Vitest npx vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=vitest.json (or equipment: vitest) Jest-style JSON, labelled vitest Playwright npx playwright test --reporter=json (PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE=results.json) Playwright JSON: retries, flaky tests, traces Cypress npx cypress run --reporter junit (or equipment: cypress) JUnit XML Mocha, WebdriverIO their junit reporter JUnit XML JUnit 4/5, TestNG, Kotest (Maven, Gradle) built in: target/surefire-reports/*.xml, build/test-results/**/*.xml JUnit XML .NET (xUnit, NUnit, MSTest) dotnet test --logger trx TRX: data rows one result each Go go test -json ./... > go-test.json go test -json: subtests, build failures as broken Rust cargo nextest run --profile ci with JUnit output configured JUnit XML PHPUnit, Pest --log-junit junit.xml JUnit XML RSpec rspec --format progress --format json --out rspec.json RSpec JSON: failure class and backtrace, pending examples as skipped, load errors as broken Minitest minitest-reporters JUnit XML XCTest, Swift Testing (Xcode 16+) xcrun xcresulttool get test-results tests --path Tests.xcresult > xcresult.json after xcodebuild test -resultBundlePath Tests.xcresult xcresulttool JSON: failure messages, retries flagged flaky Android instrumentation (Espresso, UI Automator, Compose) built in: ./gradlew connectedAndroidTest writes app/build/outputs/androidTest-results/connected/**/*.xml JUnit XML, labelled android with the device it ran on k6 k6 run --summary-export=k6-summary.json script.js (or JSON.stringify(data) from handleSummary) k6 summary: each check and each threshold is one result Robot Framework robot (writes output.xml) Robot output.xml: tags, failure messages GoogleTest, Catch2 --gtest_output=xml:gtest.xml, -r junit JUnit XML Anything with an Allure adapter its allure-results/ folder Allure results, with their attachments

A file that is none of these is skipped with a note in the stage log. See Runner Coverage - 2026-10-26.

Exit codes follow testo run: 0 every test passed or was skipped, 1 a test failed or broke, or every matching file was unreadable (truncated, empty, not a report), 2 bad arguments or no file matched, 3 the server could not be reached or refused the upload (wrong token). With --server, the job's CI provenance (provider, pipeline, job, commit, branch, repository) is sent with the files. Under the hood this is a one-stage cycle with equipment: junit run through CycleRunService; see Ingest and Team Server - 2026-10-22. For Playwright JSON (each retry as a step, flaky tests flagged, traces and screenshots copied from inside --repo as Allure attachments) see Playwright JSON Import - 2026-10-22.

docs.title: testo report
docs.text:
Build unified Allure reports from artifacts; subcommands for archives and native framework HTML.

# Default: generate + local Allure dashboard (opens browser unless --no-open)
testo report --cycle sample-pytests

testo report --generate-only --out artifacts/report
testo report --format json --summary-out summary.json
testo report list
testo report open --id <uuid>
testo report compare
testo report native
testo report native flow-tests --no-open
testo report pyramid <run-id>

docs.title: Default callback options
docs.text:
Flag Short Default Description --artifacts -a artifacts Artifacts root --cycle latest Restrict to one cycle --generate-only false Write HTML only; no HTTP server --host 127.0.0.1 Allure dashboard host --port 8080 Port (auto-picks free port if busy; 0 = always free) --out -o artifacts/report Generated HTML output dir --format -f html html, json, or junit --summary-out Path for json/junit summary file --no-history false Skip injecting prior Allure history --open / --no-open open Start dashboard after generate --trend 1 Merge history from N prior archived runs

Typical success output: messages about collecting results, running allure generate, and a local URL such as http://127.0.0.1:8080/....

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text: Command Purpose testo report list Table of archived runs (needs DB); columns: id, cycle, created, exit, tests, pass, fail testo report open --id <uuid> Extract archive and regenerate/serve Allure testo report compare Rich diff + Allure comparison (optional baseline/current UUIDs) testo report native [ROUTINE] List or open BehaveX/pytest native HTML under stage dirs testo report markdown [--cycle NAME \| --run-id ID] [--out FILE] [--run-url URL] [--baseline-branch BRANCH] The cycle's latest run (or one run) as GitHub-flavored Markdown: headline counts, per-stage table, failing tests, and per-test changes since its baseline: the latest run on --baseline-branch, else on the pull request's recorded target branch (ci_base_ref), else the cycle's previous run. When the run stored coverage, the headline adds it and its change against the same baseline (coverage 81.2% (▼ 0.4)). The first line is a hidden <!-- testo-summary:<cycle> --> marker. Exit 2 when no run is recorded. The GitHub Action uses it for the job summary and the PR comment testo report annotations [--cycle NAME \| --run-id ID] [--workspace DIR] [--limit N] [-c CONFIG] The run's failing tests as GitHub Actions ::error file=…,line=… workflow commands, so each failure shows on its line in the pull request's "Files changed". The location is the first stack-trace frame inside --workspace (default .), tried relative to the workspace, each stage's target_repo from the config, and the run's target repo. At most --limit (default 10, GitHub's per-step cap) lines, then a ::notice with the rest. Exit 2 when no run is recorded. The GitHub Action prints it by default. See Alerts Where Developers Look - 2026-10-22 testo report pyramid RUN_ID [-c CONFIG] ASCII unit/integration/e2e test pyramid for a completed run (run_id, not the archive UUID); stage→tier is the stage's tier: (default inferred from equipment: pytest→unit, behave→integration, behavex→e2e, playwright→e2e, jest→unit, vitest→unit, cypress→e2e) as recorded in the run when it executed; -c is only read for older runs that predate recorded tiers. See Architecture Overview § Test pyramid.

docs.title: testo cycles (alias: testo plans)
docs.text:
Inspect cycles in config (hidden alias plans for backward compatibility).

testo cycles list
testo cycles show sample-pytests
testo cycles show sample-pytests -c ./testosterone.yaml

list: Rich table — Name, Description, stage count.

show: Cycle title plus table of stages (equipment, target repo, args, timeout).

Config errors print [fail]config error: … and exit 2.

docs.title: testo config
docs.text:
Subcommand Description testo config validate Load YAML; optional --check-executables for pytest/behave/behavex (and npx for playwright, jest, vitest and cypress) on PATH testo config init Write starter testosterone.yaml with one active smoke-test cycle running pytest -q tests and commented-out marker/BehaveX examples (--path, --force) testo config db Set database.url (PostgreSQL prompts or --url) 
testo config validate
testo config validate --no-check-executables
testo config init --path testosterone.yaml --force
testo config db --url sqlite:////tmp/testo-reports.db

Validate success:

ok — version=1 cycles=6 reporters=4 defaults_target=.

Deprecated: testo config-db → use testo config db.

docs.title: Editor autocomplete
docs.text:
schema/testosterone.schema.json is a JSON Schema for testosterone.yaml. Editors with a YAML language server (VS Code with the Red Hat YAML extension, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim) then suggest keys and built-in equipment, and underline typos as you type. testo config init and testo init add this line at the top of the file; add it yourself to an existing config:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/taltal-beep/testosterone/main/schema/testosterone.schema.json

testo config validate is still the final word. The schema describes the cycles: layout only, and accepts plugin equipment and reporter names. Why and how it is generated: Config JSON Schema.

docs.title: testo diff / testo summary
docs.text:
Compare two archived report runs by UUID (from testo report list).

testo diff <BASELINE_ID> <CURRENT_ID>
testo summary   # same family; see help for metrics-only variants

Rich terminal diff of metrics and (for full diff) extracted Allure deltas. Reads the run history database (SQLite by default; testo-core[db] for Postgres).

Prefer testo report compare for Rich diff plus Allure visual comparison pipeline.

Note: this operates on ReportArchive UUIDs (testo report list), a separate id space from run-history run_ids — see Architecture Overview § Persistence. The React Compare page (GET /api/v1/analytics/delta + /analytics/delta/cases) reaches equivalent per-stage and per-test detail by run_id instead, per Delta Comparison Policy.

docs.title: testo flaky
docs.text:
Tests whose outcome keeps flipping across a cycle's recent runs.

testo flaky --cycle fake-api               # last 20 runs
testo flaky --cycle fake-api --window 50 --json
testo flaky --cycle nightly --fail-on-flaky  # exit 1 when any test is flaky and not quarantined (CI gate)
testo flaky --cycle nightly --new --json     # only tests the latest run made flaky
Flag Default Meaning --cycle required Cycle whose run history to read --window 20 How many of the cycle's most recent runs to look at (min 2) --new off Only tests the cycle's latest run made flaky: flaky in the window ending at that run, not in the window ending at the run before. Used for alerts and the action's flaky-issues --json off Print the report as JSON --fail-on-flaky off Exit 1 when any flaky test that isn't quarantined is found --config discovery testosterone.yaml whose quarantine: rules mark tests; without a config found, nothing is marked. Exit 2 if the given file is missing or invalid

A test is flaky when, within the window, it both passed and failed and its outcome changed at least twice (skipped runs are ignored). One change is a regression or a fix, which testo summary shows. Exit 2 when fewer than two runs with per-test results exist. Reads run-history records (run_ids) and each run's artifact snapshot, the same data as GET /api/v1/analytics/flaky?cycle=<name> and the Flaky tests card on the cycle page. See Open Source Features - 2026-10-19.

The table's Quarantined column (and "quarantined" in --json) shows which flaky tests match the cycle's quarantine: rules; for the others it prints a quarantine: snippet to paste. A quarantined test's failures don't fail testo run; see Flaky Test Quarantine - 2026-10-22.

docs.title: testo ui
docs.text:
Open the web UI (Dashboard, Cycles, Runs, Compare, AI settings) on this machine's run history: the same database and ./.testo/ data the CLI uses.

pip install 'testo-core[api]'
testo ui                     # http://127.0.0.1:8000, opens the browser
testo ui --port 9000 --no-open
Flag Default Meaning --port, -p 8000 Port on 127.0.0.1 --open / --no-open --open Open the default browser once the server is up

It starts testo-api bound to 127.0.0.1 only (for a shared server use the Team Server) and serves the UI that ships inside the wheel, or the build TESTO_UI_DIR points at. The UI's own origin (http://127.0.0.1:<port>, http://localhost:<port>) is added to TESTO_CORS_ORIGINS for this process so it can start runs; every other origin is still refused. Exit 2 when the [api] extra is missing or no built UI is found (a source checkout builds one with scripts/build_ui_bundle.sh, which needs Node 22).

docs.title: testo notify
docs.text:
Send a recorded run to Slack and/or Microsoft Teams: pass/fail counts, then new regressions, newly flaky tests, failing tests and fixed tests (10 names per list).

export TESTO_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=...         # from a secret, never on the command line
testo notify --to slack --cycle nightly                      # only when it needs attention
testo notify --to slack --to teams --cycle nightly --when change --run-url "$CI_JOB_URL"
testo notify --to teams --cycle nightly --dry-run            # print the payload, send nothing
testo notify --to slack --digest week --run-url https://testo.example.com   # weekly digest (cron)
Flag Default Meaning --to required slack or teams; repeat for both. URLs come from TESTO_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL and TESTO_TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL --cycle / --run-id latest run Which recorded run to send --when failure failure: the run failed or made a test flaky. change: the run's result flipped, or a test regressed, got fixed or became flaky. always: every run --title cycle name Name in the message --run-url none "View run" link --dry-run off Print the JSON payloads instead of posting --digest none week or day: instead of one run, a digest of every cycle (or --cycle) over that period against the one before: runs, green builds, test pass rate, line coverage, tests that turned flaky, still fail, got fixed or got slower. --run-url becomes the "Open Testosterone" link; --when and --run-id don't apply. Run it from cron or a scheduled CI job; a period with no runs sends nothing

Exit 0 when sent or when there is nothing to report, 2 for a bad flag, a missing webhook variable or no recorded run, 3 when a webhook rejects the message or can't be reached (the error never includes the URL). The slack and teams reporters send the same message right after testo run. See Alerts Where Developers Look - 2026-10-22.

docs.title: testo otel
docs.text:
Send a recorded run to an OpenTelemetry collector as one trace: a span for the run, one per stage and one per test, with the tests' real start and stop times. Failed tests, red stages and red runs are error spans. Datadog, Grafana Tempo, Honeycomb, Jaeger and any other OTLP backend show it. Needs pip install 'testo-core[otel]'.

export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://otlp.example:4318
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS="api-key=$OTLP_KEY"   # from a secret, never on the command line
testo otel --cycle nightly                               # the cycle's latest run
testo otel --run-id 3f2c... --service-name shop-tests
testo otel --cycle nightly --dry-run                     # print the spans as JSON, send nothing
Flag Default Meaning --cycle / --run-id latest run Which recorded run to send --endpoint $OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, else localhost OTLP endpoint; a base URL gets /v1/traces added for HTTP --protocol $OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL, else http/protobuf http/protobuf or grpc (grpc needs opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc) --service-name $OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, else testosterone The trace's service.name --dry-run off Print the spans as JSON instead of sending (no extra needed)

Headers come only from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS (or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADERS). Exit 0 when sent, 2 for no recorded run, a bad --protocol, an HTTP endpoint without http:// or https://, or a missing [otel] extra, 3 when the endpoint refuses the spans or can't be reached. The otel reporter sends the same trace right after testo run. Span names and attributes: OpenTelemetry Export - 2026-10-30.

docs.title: testo badge
docs.text:
A README badge for a cycle's latest run: tests | 412 passed · 2 flaky. Green when everything passed, yellow when the cycle has flaky tests (testo flaky's window), red when a test failed or broke, grey with no run.

testo badge --cycle web --out public/testo-badge.svg     # in CI, next to a published report
testo badge --cycle web --format json --out public/testo-badge.json   # a shields.io endpoint badge
Flag Default Meaning --cycle latest run of any cycle Which cycle's latest run --out / -o stdout File to write (folders are created) --format svg svg: the image. json: what https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=<its URL> reads, for shields.io's styles and logos --label tests Left-hand text

Exit 0, or 2 for a bad --format. A team server serves the same badge live at GET /api/v1/badge.svg?cycle=web and GET /api/v1/badge.json?cycle=web (cached 5 minutes). Those are reads like any other: with TESTO_PROTECT_READS on, a public README can't load them, so publish the file testo badge writes instead. Put it in a README with:

[![tests](https://you.github.io/project/testo-badge.svg)](https://you.github.io/project/)

docs.title: testo doctor
docs.text:
Health check: config load, framework CLIs on PATH, Node.js + Allure Report 3 CLI, optional Docker warnings, DB probe if DATABASE_URL or config URL is set.

testo doctor
testo doctor -c testosterone.yaml

Output: Rich table with Check / Status / Detail rows (PASS, FAIL, WARN, SKIP).

Exits 2 on hard failures (config or missing required executables) — see Troubleshooting and Error Codes § Commands that use exit codes.

docs.title: testo plugins
docs.text:
Lists the built-in frameworks and reporters, then every installed plugin with the package that registered it.

testo plugins            # table
testo plugins --check    # also import each plugin and verify its interface
testo plugins --json

Exits 1 when --check finds a plugin that fails to import or does not implement its interface; otherwise 0.

docs.title: testo clean
docs.text:
Remove artifacts/ (from config or ./artifacts) and ./temp; optional Docker prune.

testo clean --yes
testo clean -y --docker

Without --yes / -y: refuses with exit 2. It also refuses (exit 2, nothing deleted) when the artifacts root or --temp-dir is the filesystem root, your home folder, the current folder, the config's folder, a parent of any of them, or a folder holding .git, testosterone.yaml or pyproject.toml, so artifacts_root: . can't delete the project.

docs.title: testo watch
docs.text:
Filesystem watcher (watchdog) re-runs a cycle after debounced changes.

testo watch --cycle sample-pytests
testo watch --cycle sample-pytests --path sample_target_repo --debounce-ms 750

Ignores .git, artifacts, venv, __pycache__, etc. Each batch invokes testo run with the same cycle.

docs.title: testo init
docs.text:
Interactive wizard for testosterone.yaml (non-interactive alternative: testo config init).

testo init

docs.title: testo users
docs.text:
Accounts for a team server that runs with TESTO_AUTH=accounts (Team Server § Accounts). It writes to the database in DATABASE_URL, so run it where the server's database is reachable (for the compose file: docker compose exec server testo users …).

Command Effect testo users add NAME [--role viewer\|runner\|admin] [--password-stdin] Create an account (default role viewer). Prompts for the password twice unless --password-stdin; at least 10 characters testo users list Usernames, roles and creation dates testo users set-role NAME ROLE Change the role testo users reset-password NAME [--password-stdin] Set a new password testo users sign-out NAME Sign the account out of every browser testo users remove NAME Delete the account (its audit log lines stay)

set-role, reset-password and sign-out all end the account's existing sessions. Exit code 2 for a bad name, password or role, or an unknown account.

docs.title: testo lease
docs.text:
Give each parallel worker its own key from a resource pool (resources: in testosterone.yaml), so no two workers, on this machine or on other laptops, use the same VM, device or account at once. Guide: Shared Resource Pools.

testo lease run flow-vms -- pytest tests/flows      # hold a key while the command runs
testo lease run flow-vms -l win11 --wait 10m -- ./run_flow.sh
LEASE=$(testo lease take flow-vms --ttl 2h)          # prints "<key> <lease id>"
testo lease heartbeat "${LEASE#* }"; testo lease release "${LEASE#* }"
testo lease list                                     # who holds what, how many wait
Command Effect testo lease run POOL [-l LABEL] [--wait 30m] [--note TEXT] -- CMD... Wait for a key, run CMD with TESTO_RESOURCE_ID, TESTO_RESOURCE_POOL, TESTO_RESOURCE_LABELS, TESTO_RESOURCE_DATA, TESTO_RESOURCE_<NAME> per data value and TESTO_LEASE_ID set, heartbeat while it runs, give the key back when it ends. Exits with CMD's exit code testo lease take POOL [-l LABEL] [--wait 30m] [--ttl DURATION] [--json] Take a key and print <key> <lease id> (or JSON with the env vars). Nothing heartbeats it: it lives --ttl (default the pool's lease_ttl) unless you call heartbeat testo lease heartbeat LEASE_ID Keep a lease alive for another TTL. Exit 1 when it is gone testo lease release LEASE_ID [--clean] Give the key back. --clean: you reset it yourself, so the next taker gets TESTO_RESOURCE_CLEAN=1 testo lease list [POOL] [--json] Each pool's keys: free (and whether it was left clean), held (by whom, since when), expired (free again after the pool's reuse_delay) or disabled, and how many requests wait testo lease disable POOL KEY [--reason TEXT] / enable POOL KEY Take a broken key out of the pool, put it back testo lease free POOL KEY Take a key back from its holder (needs admin on a server with accounts) testo lease demo [--clear] Fill this machine's database with made-up pools (demo-flow-vms, demo-phones, demo-license-seats), some keys held by invented people, one disabled and two requests waiting, to try testo lease list and the Resources page. Never touches a team server. --clear gives the keys back Flag Default Meaning -l, --label none Only keys with this label; repeat for several --wait 30m How long to wait for a free key: 90s, 10m, 2h, 0 (try once) or forever --server $TESTO_SERVER_URL Team server that keeps the leases (token from $TESTO_API_TOKEN). Unset: this machine's run-history database --config discovery testosterone.yaml with the pools

Exit codes: 2 for an unknown pool, a bad config or no command after --; 3 when no key came free within --wait, the pool has no usable key (none match the labels, or all are disabled), or the server can't be reached; 1 when heartbeat or disable/enable/free finds nothing to act on.

docs.title: testo pool
docs.text:
Compare resource pools with the keys that really exist, and add or remove keys with the pool's own provider commands. Testosterone never creates or deletes a key on its own: add, remove and sweep are dry runs unless --apply. Guide: Shared Resource Pools.

Command Effect testo pool status [POOL] [--check] [--json] Read-only. For each pool: which keys provider.list shows (yes, missing, or ? without a list command), which listed keys aren't in the pool, and each key's lease state. --check runs on_check on every free key that exists testo pool add POOL [KEY...] [-n N] [--apply] [--yes] Make keys with provider.create: the names given, or N names <name_prefix><n>. Stops at max_items. Doesn't edit your config testo pool remove POOL KEY... [--apply] [--yes] Remove keys with provider.destroy. Skips keys in items, held keys, names without name_prefix and keys provider.list doesn't show testo pool sweep POOL [--apply] [--yes] Remove leftovers: keys provider.list shows with name_prefix that aren't in the pool or held, 5 at a time testo pool log [POOL] [--limit 20] [--json] Every create/destroy run with --apply: when, which key, who and from where, and how it went

add, remove and sweep print the commands and run nothing without --apply; with it they ask first unless --yes. They need the verb under provider.allow, take at most 5 keys per command, and are refused when TESTO_PROVIDER_ACTIONS=0.

Flags --server and --config as for testo lease. Exit codes: 0 done (or a dry run), or every pool matches for status; 1 a key is missing, not in the pool or fails its check (status), or a command failed or every key was skipped (add/remove/sweep, also when you answer no); 2 an unknown pool, a bad config, a verb that isn't allowed, too many keys, or TESTO_PROVIDER_ACTIONS=0; 3 a provider.list command failed, the lease server can't be reached, or a command ran but logging it failed (nothing more runs).

docs.title: testo split
docs.text:
Split a cycle's tests into shards that take about the same time, from each test's median time over the cycle's recent runs (longest test first, each to the shard with the least time so far). For CI matrix jobs, or one shard per key of a pool. Guide: Shared Resource Pools § Split tests by time.

testo split --cycle flows --shards 4                       # table: tests and time per shard
pytest --collect-only -q | testo split --cycle flows --shards 4 --index 2 --tests -   # shard 2's node ids
testo split --cycle flows --shards 4 --json                # every shard, with its tests
Flag Default Meaning --cycle required Cycle whose test times to use --shards required How many shards --index I none Print only shard I's tests (1 to --shards), one per line --tests FILE the cycle's history Tests to split, one per line (- reads stdin). pytest node ids are matched to their recorded names --stage all Only this stage's tests --server $TESTO_SERVER_URL Read the times from a team server (token from $TESTO_API_TOKEN) --window 20 Recent runs to take the times from

Tests with no recorded time count as a typical (median) test; with no history at all the split is round robin. The split depends only on which tests there are and their times, not their order, so every shard that sees the same history picks the same tests. Exit codes: 2 for a bad --index or unreadable --tests, 3 when the server can't be reached, 1 when there is nothing to split.

docs.title: testo affected
docs.text:
Pick the tests a change can affect, and say why each one was picked. Opt-in: nothing runs fewer tests unless you use this command or pytest --testo-affected. Design: Affected Test Selection - 2026-10-30.

testo affected                                   # tests to run, each with its reasons
testo affected --base origin/develop --json      # the selection, reasons and per-file decisions
npx jest $(testo affected --list)                # nothing printed = run everything
git diff --name-only HEAD~1 | testo affected --changed -
Flag Default Meaning --base REF affected.base, else the pull request's target branch in CI, else origin/main Diff the working tree (and untracked files) against the merge base with this --changed FILE git diff Changed files, one per line, relative to the repo root (- reads stdin) --coverage FILE affected.coverage coverage.py JSON with test contexts: pytest --cov --cov-context=test, then coverage json --show-contexts --config discovery testosterone.yaml with the affected: section --list off Only the tests, one per line; prints nothing when everything should run --json off run_all, run_all_reasons, nothing_to_run, tests (with reasons) and files (each changed file's outcome)

Each changed file maps to tests by the first of: run_all_when (run everything), ignore (no test), a changed test file (it runs), rules, the coverage report. Anything else, an unknown base or an empty diff runs everything, with the reason. Exit codes: 0 for any selection, including "run everything"; 2 for a bad config, an unreadable --changed or --coverage, or both --list and --json.

affected:
  base: origin/main            # optional
  coverage: coverage.json      # optional, relative to this file
  run_all_when: ["src/core/**"]   # added to conftest.py, pyproject.toml, lockfiles, testosterone.yaml
  ignore: ["docs/**", "*.md"]
  test_files: ["test_*.py"]    # replaces the built-in names of test files
  rules:
    - changed: "src/payments/**"
      tests: ["tests/payments/**", "tests/test_api.py::test_checkout"]

docs.title: testo backup / testo restore
docs.text:
Copy the whole run history (every database table and each run's stored results under static/history/) into one .tar.gz, and load it back, into the same or another database (SQLite, Postgres, MySQL).

testo backup                                   # ./testo-backup-<date>-<time>.tar.gz
testo backup --out /backups/testo.tar.gz --no-files
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://... testo restore testo-backup-20261101-090000.tar.gz
testo restore old.tar.gz --replace --yes       # delete the current history first
Flag Default Meaning backup --out / -o testo-backup-<UTC time>.tar.gz Where to write it (written as .partial, then renamed) backup --no-files off Tables only, without the per-run result snapshots (Compare, flaky and the test page need those for old runs) restore PATH required A file testo backup wrote restore --replace off Empty the tables first. Without it, a database that already has runs is refused restore --yes / -y off Don't ask before --replace

Only columns today's tables have are written, so an older backup restores into a newer version. The AI settings file (it holds API keys) is never included; the user_account table holds password hashes, so keep backups as private as the database. Exit 0 on success, 2 for a file that isn't a backup or a database that already has runs, 3 when the database can't be reached.

docs.title: testo version
docs.text:
testo version
# testo 0.1.0

# Equivalent top-level eager flag (works before/instead of a subcommand):
testo --version
testo -v

docs.title: pytest --testo
docs.text:
testo-core installs a pytest plugin (entry point pytest11, testo_core/pytest_plugin.py). It does nothing unless asked:

Option Effect --testo Record this session as a run (also TESTO_RECORD=1) --testo-cycle NAME Cycle to record under; implies --testo. Default: the rootdir's name --testo-tier unit\|integration\|e2e Pyramid tier of the tests (default unit) --testo-server URL Upload to a team server instead (default $TESTO_SERVER_URL, token from $TESTO_API_TOKEN) --testo-resource POOL Give each worker its own key from this resource pool (from testosterone.yaml, or $TESTO_RESOURCE_SPEC set by a stage's resources:). Tests read it from the variables or the testo_resource fixture --testo-resource-per worker\|test One key per worker (default) or a fresh one per test --testo-resource-label LABEL Only keys with this label (repeat for more) --testo-resource-wait DURATION How long to wait for a key (default 30m); then the test fails --testo-shard I/N Run only shard I of N, split by time like testo split (also $TESTO_SHARD). Bad value or unreachable server: usage error (exit 4), never a guess --testo-affected Run only the tests the changes since the baseline branch can affect, like testo affected (also $TESTO_AFFECTED=1); deselects the rest before --testo-shard splits. The summary lists what was picked and why, or why everything ran. A picked Python test that isn't collected runs everything; when only ignored files changed, no test runs and pytest exits 0 --testo-affected-base REF Branch or commit --testo-affected diffs against (default as testo affected --base) --testo-failed-first Run the tests that failed last time first, then flaky ones, then ones that failed in the last 20 runs, then the rest in pytest's order (also $TESTO_FAILED_FIRST=1). History comes from the same cycle as --testo-timings (local, or --testo-server). Applies after --testo-affected and --testo-shard; works with pytest-xdist. The summary says how many moved; when no history can be read, pytest's order is kept --testo-timings CYCLE Cycle whose test times --testo-shard uses (default $TESTO_CYCLE, which testo run sets, else the rootdir's name; from --testo-server / $TESTO_SERVER_URL when set)

The session's JUnit XML (yours if --junitxml is set, else a temporary file in a .testo-* folder of the rootdir, removed afterwards) is recorded through the same path as testo ingest, into a pytest stage, and the run writes artifacts/ like testo ingest does. One line in pytest's summary says where it went. Recording never changes pytest's exit code: a problem is reported on that line instead. Nothing is recorded when no tests ran, or on a pytest-xdist worker (the controller records).

docs.title: Other entry points (not testo Typer tree)
docs.text:
Command Package Role testo-api testo_api FastAPI server (React UI backend)

The v1.0 uqo command (including its uqo run --config headless format with --ghost, --json, --stream-json) and the testo-ui Streamlit app were removed in v1.1; use testo run --cycle … --ci and the React frontend.

docs.title: Environment variables (common)
docs.text: Variable Effect DATABASE_URL Overrides database.url in YAML for archives / list TESTO_HOME Where per-run report copies (static/, static_reports/) are written. Default: ./.testo for a pip install, the repository root for a source checkout (Architecture Overview § Artifact layout) INFLUXDB_URL, INFLUXDB_TOKEN, INFLUXDB_ORG, INFLUXDB_BUCKET Push run KPIs to InfluxDB after each run PROMETHEUS_PUSHGATEWAY_URL, PROMETHEUS_JOB_NAME Push run KPIs to a Prometheus Pushgateway after each run TESTO_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL, TESTO_TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL Webhooks for testo notify and the slack / teams reporters OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL, OTEL_SERVICE_NAME Where testo otel and the otel reporter send traces (the standard OpenTelemetry variables, *_TRACES_* forms too) TESTO_SERVER_URL, TESTO_API_TOKEN Team server for testo lease (and pytest --testo-server) TESTO_LEASE_DB_URL Database for local leases when it isn't the run-history one TESTO_SHARD I/N: run only that shard of a pytest session (--testo-shard) TESTO_REDACT 0 turns off hiding secrets in a run's stored results and logs (on by default: API keys, tokens, passwords, credentials in URLs, private keys) TESTO_REDACT_PATTERNS Your own regular expressions to hide, one per line TESTO_FAILED_FIRST 1: same as --testo-failed-first TESTO_CYCLE, TESTO_STAGE Set by testo run for each stage's process: which cycle and stage it is Reporter tokens e.g. REPORTPORTAL_TOKEN, SLACK_WEBHOOK via ${env:…} in YAML

docs.title: Reporter types (reporters: / --reporter)
docs.text:
Supported: allure, extent, otel, reportportal, slack, teams, testbeats, plus any installed reporter plugin. Configured in root testosterone.yaml; outputs often under reports/ (see repo testosterone.yaml for examples).

slack and teams post the testo notify message for the run that just finished. They need a recorded run (not --no-persist):

reporters:
  - type: slack
    webhook: ${env:SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL}   # default: $TESTO_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL
    when: failure                        # failure | change | always
    title: Nightly API tests             # default: the cycle name
    report_url: ${env:CI_JOB_URL}        # optional "View run" link

otel sends the testo otel trace for the run that just finished (recorded runs only, [otel] extra). Options left out fall back to the OTEL_* variables:

reporters:
  - type: otel
    endpoint: https://otlp.example:4318   # default: $OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
    headers: ${env:OTLP_HEADERS}          # "key=value,..."; default: $OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS
    protocol: http/protobuf               # or grpc
    service_name: shop-tests              # default: $OTEL_SERVICE_NAME or testosterone

testbeats posts counts only, to the slack_webhook / teams_webhook options.

After testo run, terminal hints may point to ./reports/allure, ./reports/extent, etc.

docs.title: Official documentation
docs.text: Reporter Reference Allure Report 3 https://allurereport.org/docs/v3/ ReportPortal https://reportportal.io/docs/api-development/ ReportPortal agents https://reportportal.io/docs/log-data-in-reportportal/test-framework-integration/

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
A Python package can add a test runner (equipment:) or a reporter (reporters:) without changing Testosterone, through two entry point groups:

# the plugin's pyproject.toml
[project.entry-points."testo.frameworks"]
unittest = "testo_example_plugin:UnittestAdapter"

[project.entry-points."testo.reporters"]
json-summary = "testo_example_plugin:JsonSummaryReporter"

After pip install, the names work in testosterone.yaml and --reporter, and testo plugins lists them.

Group Value Interface testo.frameworks A class or factory returning an adapter FrameworkAdapter in testo_core/frameworks/base.py: name, results_subdir(), build_argv(target_repo, results_dir, stage_args, workers) and native_report(stage_dir) testo.reporters A BaseReporter subclass testo_core/reporting/reporters/base.py: reporter_type and publish(results, context, console); YAML keys other than type arrive as self._options
  • The stage process runs build_argv's command in target_repo. Tests are counted from Allure *-result.json files written to results_dir (also exported as TESTO_SHARED_ALLURE_RESULTS_DIR), or from the stage's junit_xml globs.
  • A plugin stage defaults to tier: unit and gets workers passed through unchanged.
  • Built-in names always win; a plugin that reuses one, or a second plugin with the same name, is ignored with a warning.
  • Plugins are imported only when a stage or reporter uses them, or by testo plugins --check.
  • The API's ad-hoc run endpoint (POST /api/v1/adhoc-executions) accepts built-in frameworks only.

examples/plugin is a complete plugin with one of each. Design: Plugin API.

docs.text:
• CI-CD Pipeline Setup — testo run --ci in CI wrappers
  • Delta Comparison Policy — semantics for testo diff / testo summary

docs.title: Troubleshooting and Error Codes
docs.text:
Command Reference

Practical guide for debugging testo failures: exit codes, CI payloads, log locations, and step-by-step fixes. Implementation detail: Deep Dive - Execution Logic.

docs.title: Exit code reference
docs.text:
Defined in testo_core/engine/exit_codes.py as EngineExitCode. The process exit code is propagated via typer.Exit in command handlers and testo_core/cli/app.py main().

Code Enum Meaning Typical causes 0 SUCCESS Run completed; all stage return codes zero Pass; or cycle skipped by trigger (resting) 1 DOMAIN_FAILURE Tests or framework reported failure Non-zero pytest/behave/behavex exit 2 INVALID_INPUT Config or CLI validation failed Missing YAML, bad schema, unknown cycle, tag mismatch; a mistyped command or option, or bare testo (prints the error or the help, no traceback) 3 INFRA_FAILURE Infrastructure / runtime dependency failure Return code 127 (missing binary); 124 (stage timeout); report DB archive failure; Docker/Allure CLI failures 4 INTERNAL_ERROR Unexpected engine error Orchestrator internal_failure on uncaught engine exception; empty return-code list in classifier

docs.title: Classification logic
docs.text:
classify_exit_code(returncodes, infra_error=None, internal_failure=False):

  • infra_error set → 3
  • internal_failure set → 4 (orchestrator caught an unexpected engine exception; not a framework subprocess exit)
  • Empty returncodes → 4
  • Any stage return code in (124, 127) → 3
  • Any other non-zero return code → 1
  • Otherwise → 0

Stage timeouts emit returncode=124 and timed_out=true. Engine internal failures set internal_failure=true on the stage result (NDJSON stage_finished includes both fields).

docs.title: Commands that use exit codes
docs.text: Command Uses EngineExitCode testo run Yes — engine result testo ingest Yes — engine result locally; with --server, the server's result, or 3 when the upload fails (unreachable, wrong token) testo report Yes — missing artifacts, Allure failure, I/O errors testo doctor 2 on hard FAIL; 0 on pass testo config validate 2 on failure (literal in some handlers) testo clean 2 / 3 testo config db 2 / 3

docs.title: Interactive (default)
docs.text:
• Config errors: [fail]error: <message>
  • Run failure: Run exited with code <N>.
  • Success: Run finished successfully.
  • Trigger skip: Rich panel titled Resting
  • Stage failure: post-mortem panel with output_tail and log path

docs.title: CI (--ci)
docs.text:
All machine-readable lines go to stdout as NDJSON (one JSON object per line). No Rich markup.

Config error:

{"event":"error","code":"invalid_input","message":"cycle 'foo' not found. Available: bar, baz."}

Trigger evaluation:

{"event":"cycle_trigger","cycle":"sample-pytests","status":"resting","reason":"...","matched":[],"mode":"git"}

Dry run skip (roadmap — no --dry-run CLI flag exists yet, see Command Reference):

{"event":"dry_run","cycle":"sample-pytests","status":"skipped","reason":"trigger"}

Stdout is reserved for NDJSON in CI mode — do not pipe other tools onto the same stream without filtering.

docs.title: Artifact mirror
docs.text: artifacts/<cycle>/events.ndjson duplicates engine events (plan_started, stage_started, stage_finished, plan_finished, plan_aborted) even in interactive mode. Use this file when CI logs are truncated.

docs.title: NDJSON event schema (testo run --ci)
docs.text: Emitted by CIRenderer and _NdjsonRecorder.

docs.title: plan_started
docs.text: {"event":"plan_started","plan":"sample-pytests","stage_count":1}

docs.title: stage_started
docs.text: {"event":"stage_started","stage":"pytest-sample","framework":"pytest","index":1,"count":1}

docs.title: stage_finished
docs.text:
{
  "event":"stage_finished",
  "stage":"pytest-sample",
  "framework":"pytest",
  "returncode":1,
  "duration_s":12.4,
  "log_path":"/path/artifacts/sample-pytests/pytest-sample/run.log",
  "timed_out":false
}

When the executor sets an error string (timeout, missing binary):

  • error may appear on the in-memory result; the NDJSON mirror in orchestrator includes error when present on StageResult. The mirror also carries internal_failure (true only for orchestrator-caught engine exceptions). CIRenderer stdout omits both keys.

docs.title: plan_finished
docs.text:
{
  "event":"plan_finished",
  "plan":"sample-pytests",
  "aggregate_returncode":1,
  "exit_code":1,
  "duration_s":12.5,
  "stages":[...],
  "error":null
}

docs.title: plan_aborted (engine fail_fast)
docs.text:
Written to the artifact events.ndjson when run_plan(fail_fast=True) aborts after a failing stage. Reachable today via the API layer (POST /api/v1/cycles/{cycle}/executions); the --fail-fast CLI flag is a roadmap item.

{"event":"plan_aborted","plan":"sample-pytests","reason":"fail_fast","completed_stages":1}

docs.title: Log and artifact map
docs.text:
artifacts/<cycle>/
  events.ndjson              # Full event timeline
  plan_result.json           # Summary JSON (best-effort)
  <stage>/
    run.log                  # Complete subprocess stdout+stderr
    allure-results/
      pytest/ | behave/ | behavex/
        *-result.json

Post-run reports (when configured): often under reports/allure/, reports/extent/, etc. — see testosterone.yaml reporters:.

Report DB archives: require testo-core[db] and database.url or DATABASE_URL; UUID from testo report list.

docs.title: Config not found (exit 2)
docs.text:
Symptoms

error: no testosterone.yaml / testosterone.yml / pyproject.toml [tool.testosterone] found under /your/cwd

Debug

  1. Confirm working directory: pwd
  2. Or pass explicit path: testo run --cycle <name> --config /path/to/testosterone.yaml
  3. CI: parse NDJSON {"event":"error","code":"invalid_input",...}

Fix

  • Add testosterone.yaml at repo root or set --config
  • Use testo config init / testo init to scaffold

docs.title: Invalid YAML or schema (exit 2)
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • invalid YAML in ...
  • unknown equipment 'foo'
  • Pydantic-style validation messages from loader

Debug

testo config validate
testo config validate --config path/to/testosterone.yaml

Fix

  • Correct syntax and keys per Architecture Overview § Configuration as the single source of truth
  • Supported frameworks: pytest, behave, behavex

docs.title: Unknown cycle or no enabled stages (exit 2)
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • cycle 'x' not found. Available: ...
  • the config defines several cycles; pick one with --cycle. Available: ... (testo run with no --cycle)
  • Error: No such command 'x'. or Error: No such option: --x after a Usage: line (a mistyped command or flag; also exit 2)
  • plan 'x' has no stages enabled in this environment

Debug

testo cycles list
testo cycles show <name>

Fix

  • Use a defined cycle name from cycles: in YAML
  • Check stage if_expr — stage may be disabled for current env vars

docs.title: Tag filter mismatch (exit 2)
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • cycle 'foo' does not include tag 'smoke'
  • No cycles match --tag 'smoke'

Fix

  • Add tag to cycle in YAML, or run without --tag
  • For testo run --cycle all --tag smoke, ensure at least one cycle lists smoke under tags:

docs.title: Trigger skip — resting (exit 0)
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • Panel: Cycle <name> skipped: No stimulus detected...
  • NDJSON: "status":"resting" on cycle_trigger
  • No stages run; no new failures

Debug

  • Inspect trigger: block on the cycle (paths, since_ref)
  • Snapshot state under artifacts/ for the cycle

Fix

  • Expected behavior when no matching file changes
  • Force run: testo run --cycle <name> --force

docs.title: Framework executable missing (exit 3 or 1)
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • Stage error: executable not found: ...
  • Stage returncode: 127 → should yield exit 3 at plan level
  • testo doctor shows CLI pytest FAIL — not found on PATH

Debug

testo doctor
cat artifacts/<cycle>/<stage>/run.log

Fix

  • Install framework in active venv: pip install pytest; for behave / behavex stages, pip install 'testo-core[bdd]' (since 1.2 a plain pip install testo-core leaves them out, and the stage error says so)
  • Ensure CI image activates the same venv before testo run

docs.title: Stage timeout (exit 3)
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • timed_out: true and returncode: 124 in stage_finished NDJSON / events.ndjson
  • error: stage exceeded timeout_s=<N>
  • Truncated or abrupt end in run.log
  • Process exit code 3 when timeout is the only failure

Debug

# Inspect event file
grep timed_out artifacts/<cycle>/events.ndjson
tail -100 artifacts/<cycle>/<stage>/run.log

Fix

  • Increase timeout_s in defaults: or per-stage in YAML
  • Fix hanging test; use testo run --stream locally to watch live output

docs.title: Test / assertion failures (exit 1)
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • Non-zero stage returncode (often 1)
  • Framework traceback in run.log
  • Allure *-result.json with failed status

Debug

testo run --cycle <name> --stream    # live output
testo report --cycle <name>          # Allure dashboard

Fix

  • Address failing tests in target_repo
  • Use --fail-fast to stop after first failing stage

docs.title: Allure Report 3 CLI missing (exit 3 on report)
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • testo report prints failure from AllureReporter
  • testo doctor shows Allure Report 3 CLI WARN

Debug

node --version
testo doctor
ls node_modules/.bin/allure   # after npm install in repo root

Fix

  • Install Node.js 18+, then in the Testo repo root: npm install (installs the allure npm package pinned in package.json)
  • Or set TESTO_ALLURE_BIN to a custom Allure 3 executable
  • Or use testo report --format json which does not need the Node CLI

Command mapping (Allure 2 → 3)

Allure 2 (Java) Allure 3 (Node) allure generate <dirs> -o <out> --clean allure generate <dirs> -o <out> --config ./allurerc.mjs allure generate … --single-file allure awesome <dirs> -o <out> --single-file allure serve <dirs> allure open <dirs> --port <n> (generate + serve) allure open <reportDir> allure open <reportDir> --port <n>

Hosted reports: {ALLURE_SERVER_URL}/reports/<run_id>/index.html (any static file server).

See also: Allure Report 3 docs, Docker Engine.

docs.title: No artifacts for report (exit 2)
docs.text:
Symptoms

no results found under artifacts — run testo run --cycle … first

Debug

ls -la artifacts/<cycle>/
find artifacts -name '*-result.json' | head

Fix

  • Run the cycle first: testo run --cycle <name>
  • Match --artifacts path if non-default
  • Reporters skipped when no Allure JSON exists (see run_configured_reporters)

Run Detail page shows "No artifacts recorded" / "No reports for this run" despite a passing cycle: fixed 2026-07-06 — DbBackend.persist() never set snapshot_dir on the RunRecord, so GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/reports always returned artifact_links: []. See Report Links and Artifacts Missing Fix - 2026-07-06. Native Allure/Behave HTML static_links still require a reporters: block in testosterone.yaml — that part is a config gap, not a bug.

docs.title: Report database / archive failures (exit 3)
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • testo report list fails or doctor DB row FAIL
  • No UUID printed after run when archive expected

Debug

testo doctor
echo "$DATABASE_URL"
testo config db show    # if configured

Fix

  • Install extra: pip install 'testo-core[db]'
  • Set database.url in YAML or DATABASE_URL
  • In CI, archive always runs synchronously (--ci ignores --async-report-db)
  • A failed required archive after a green run exits 3
  • Use --no-report-db to skip archive when DB not needed

docs.title: Reporter partial failure (exit 0)
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • Tests passed but Slack/ReportPortal/Extent missing
  • [fail] lines from reporter factory but run still exits 0

Debug

  • Check reporter-specific env vars (REPORTPORTAL_TOKEN, webhooks in YAML)
  • Inspect reports/ output dirs

Fix

  • Validate reporters: block in testosterone.yaml
  • Run testo report separately to isolate Allure vs integrations

docs.title: Argparse / Typer help (non-engine)
docs.text:
Symptoms

  • Typer prints help when required options missing (e.g. testo run without --cycle)
  • May not use EngineExitCode — often exit 2 from Click/Typer

Fix

  • Pass required flags per Command Reference

docs.title: Removed: uqo run headless contract
docs.text: v1.0 shipped a second CLI contract, uqo run --config <runs.yaml> with --ghost, --json and --stream-json, backed by a Docker-based runner. It was removed in v1.1 together with the uqo command, and CI integrations use testo run --cycle <name> --ci (NDJSON events above, plan_finished last). Exit codes 0–4 mean the same thing in both.

docs.title: Quick diagnostic commands
docs.text:
testo doctor
testo config validate
testo cycles list
testo run --cycle <name> --dry-run
testo run --cycle <name> --ci 2>/dev/null | tee run.ndjson
testo run --cycle <name> --stream

docs.title: CI Integrations
docs.text: Pre-packaged CI wrappers keep orchestration in testo_core: they install testo-core, run testo run --ci, and keep its machine output.

docs.title: Architecture boundary
docs.text:
• Execution is testo run → CycleRunService → engine.run_plan(), the same path as a local run and an API execution.
  • CI wrappers are thin adapters that only prepare flags and consume the NDJSON stream.
  • CI provenance is detected from the environment by DbBackend (testo_core/services/ci_provenance.py) and stored on the run record; repository adapters stay provider-agnostic.

docs.title: Output contract in CI
docs.text:
testo run --ci writes one JSON object per line on stdout (plan_started, stage_started, stage_finished, plan_finished, plus cycle_trigger / error when relevant). The last line is plan_finished with exit_code and per-stage results. Exit codes 0–4: Troubleshooting and Error Codes.

v1.0's "ghost mode" (uqo run --config … --ghost/--json/--stream-json and a summary JSON) was removed in v1.1 together with the Docker-based headless runner it drove.

docs.title: Canonical CI provenance fields
docs.text:
Run records written in CI include (when the provider exposes them):

  • ci_provider (github, gitlab, buildkite, circleci, jenkins, azure_pipelines, generic)
  • ci_pipeline_id
  • ci_job_id
  • ci_commit_sha
  • ci_ref_name: the branch. On a GitHub pull_request event that is GITHUB_HEAD_REF (the PR's branch), not GITHUB_REF_NAME (<number>/merge)
  • ci_base_ref: a pull or merge request's target branch (GITHUB_BASE_REF, CI_MERGE_REQUEST_TARGET_BRANCH_NAME, BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST_BASE_BRANCH, Jenkins CHANGE_TARGET, Azure SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_TARGETBRANCH); unset on branch builds

Runs also record repository (owner/name, from GITHUB_REPOSITORY, CI_PROJECT_PATH, BUILDKITE_REPO or CIRCLE_PROJECT_REPONAME). Runs outside CI record git_branch and git_commit from the target repository's checkout instead, and repository when its origin remote is on github.com. testo ingest sends the same fields with the upload.

The PR comment and testo report markdown compare a pull request's run with the latest run of the same cycle on its ci_base_ref branch, so a parallel PR's run is never the baseline. With no run on that branch yet they fall back to the previous run on the run's own branch (never another pull request's), a push to the default branch is compared with the previous run on that branch, and they say which one they used ("Since the last run on main" or "Since the previous run"). Test names are shown as code spans that nothing in a name can close, so a name can't @mention anyone or render HTML in the comment. When testo run stops before recording a run (bad config), the action publishes no summary, comment, annotations or alert rather than an earlier job's run. This needs history shared between jobs (a database.url or a team server); on a fresh runner there is nothing to compare with.

docs.title: GitHub Action
docs.text:
The action is action.yml at the repository root, the copy the GitHub Marketplace lists (uses: taltal-beep/testosterone@v1, from 1.4.0); integrations/github-action/action.yml is the same action at its older path and keeps working, and tests/contract/ci/test_action_copies.py fails if the two differ. Source lives under integrations/github-action/ (inputs: config-path, cycle, ci-mode, persist, python-version, package, job-summary, comment-on-pr, annotations, slack-webhook, teams-webhook, notify-when, flaky-issues, coverage, github-token; outputs: exit_code, status, summary_json, summary_path).

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write        # only for comment-on-pr
steps:
  - uses: taltal-beep/testosterone@v1
    with:
      cycle: smoke
      comment-on-pr: "true"

After a persisted run the action renders it with testo report markdown and writes it to the job summary (job-summary, default on). With comment-on-pr: "true" on pull_request events it keeps one comment per cycle on the pull request, found by its hidden marker and edited on later pushes. Both are best-effort: an error, such as a fork's read-only token, is a workflow warning and never changes the exit code. package is what gets pip-installed (testo-core by default; testo-core[bdd] for cycles with behave or behavex stages; this repository's own CI passes .; several requirements are separated by spaces, testo-core pytest-xdist). With cycle: all every cycle gets its own job summary section, PR comment, annotations and alert. Inputs reach the action's shell steps as environment variables, never as script text, so a branch name in an input can't run commands. The GitLab template's TESTO_PACKAGE variable does the same. Design: GitHub Action PR Comment - 2026-10-19.

The action also prints failing tests as annotations on the diff (annotations, default on, no permission needed; testo report annotations). Pass slack-webhook: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }} and/or teams-webhook to get a chat alert (testo notify, notify-when default failure). flaky-issues: "true" opens one issue (label flaky-test) per test the run made flaky and needs issues: write. All three are best-effort like the summary. coverage: coverage.xml (space-separated; Cobertura, JaCoCo, LCOV or Go cover profiles your tests write) stores line coverage with the run, and the summary and PR comment show it with its change against the baseline (testo run --coverage). Design: Alerts Where Developers Look - 2026-10-22.

docs.title: GitLab include template
docs.text:
Template lives at ci/gitlab/testo.gitlab-ci.yml.

include:
  - project: "taltal-beep/testosterone"
    file: "/ci/gitlab/testo.gitlab-ci.yml"

variables:
  TESTO_CYCLE: "smoke"

Variables: TESTO_CONFIG_PATH (empty = discovery), TESTO_CYCLE (empty = the only cycle), TESTO_PERSIST (true default). Artifacts: testo-output.ndjson and testo-summary.json (the plan_finished line).

docs.title: Runner image
docs.text: Dockerfile.testo-runner builds an image whose entrypoint is testo. Use it as the CI job image when you want a pinned toolchain; stages run as subprocesses inside that job container. See Publishing Docker Images.

docs.title: Tiered test harness commands
docs.text:
Tier selection is marker-driven and shared between local runs and GitHub Actions:

  • Fast required gate:
  • python -m pytest -q -m "tier_fast and not quarantined" --maxfail=1 --no-cov
  • Heavy optional gate:
  • python -m pytest -q -m "tier_heavy and not tier_external" --maxfail=1 --durations=25
  • External nightly/release gate:
  • python -m pytest -q -m "tier_external and cleanup_required" --maxfail=1 --durations=50

Reference CI definitions:

  • GitHub: .github/workflows/ci.yml (unified pipeline: format and test run in parallel, then deploy on a release; the fast-required gate lives in its test job on Python 3.11, followed by the heavy tier, and test_python_versions runs the same suite on 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 without the coverage gate), .github/workflows/pr-heavy.yml, .github/workflows/nightly-external.yml, .github/workflows/release-gate.yml. Code review runs via a local pre-push hook (.claude/settings.json), not in CI.

All tier jobs upload diagnostics artifacts (logs, summary JSON, API responses, screenshots when present) on failure, and external suites run with external-e2e concurrency isolation.

docs.title: This repository's workflows
docs.text:
What runs on Testosterone itself, as opposed to the wrappers above that run it in other projects. Every workflow is under .github/workflows/.

Workflow Runs on What it does ci.yml pull request, push to main, release Blocking gates: ruff lint and format, mypy on testo_core and testo_api; the fast pytest suite with the coverage gate; frontend typecheck, ESLint, generated API types up to date, vitest and build; CHANGELOG.md touched; docs vault lint; the docs site with mkdocs build --strict; examples/getting-started/ through the local GitHub Action, once with the PyPI release and once with this checkout (which also posts the PR comment); builds the sdist and wheel, runs twine check --strict, installs the wheel with no extras and runs a cycle (scripts/package_smoke.sh). Builds the wheel on a release commitlint.yml pull request Conventional commit messages changelog-on-main.yml push to main Drafts a CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] entry from the pushed commits with Claude and commits it to main; skips when its bot secrets are missing pages-demo.yml push to main, nightly Runs the self-test and fake-api cycles and publishes the read-only UI and the docs site to GitHub Pages (GitLab Pages Demo) wiki-sync.yml push to main touching docs/ Regenerates the GitHub wiki from docs/ (Docs Vault and Wiki Sync) mirror-to-gitlab.yml push to main Mirrors the repo to GitLab when GITLAB_MIRROR_URL / GITLAB_MIRROR_TOKEN are set pr-heavy.yml labeled pull request, manual Heavy test tier nightly-external.yml nightly, manual External test tier release-gate.yml manual Release checks before publishing dependabot.yml (config, not a workflow) weekly Grouped dependency update PRs for pip, npm (/ and frontend/) and GitHub Actions, committed as chore(deps) with the no-changelog label so commitlint and changelog_required pass publish.yml, docker-publish.yml, artifactory-publish.yml GitHub Release published (publish.yml and docker-publish.yml can also be run by hand for an existing tag) PyPI, GHCR runner image, JFrog Artifactory (Publishing to PyPI, Publishing Docker Images) move-major-tag.yml GitHub Release published (not prereleases), manual Force-moves the v<major> tag (e.g. v1) to the release's commit

docs.title: Versioning policy
docs.text:
• GitHub action: publish immutable semver tags (v1.0.0, v1.0.1, ...), keep v1 moving to latest stable v1.x (done by move-major-tag.yml), and recommend SHA pinning for strict supply-chain policies.
  • GitLab template: pin include to immutable tag or commit SHA in production pipelines.
  • Runner image tags:
  • immutable: v1.x.y, sha-<commit>
  • moving: v1, latest
  • Compatibility rule: testo-runner:v1.x.y must embed a testo-core 1.x.y compatible CLI contract (testo run --ci NDJSON and exit semantics).

docs.title: E2E Harness Operations
docs.text: This document defines deterministic execution and cleanup for the tiered E2E harness.

docs.title: Flow lifecycle
docs.text:
All flow scenarios follow:

  1. provision
  2. execute
  3. poll
  4. verify
  5. cleanup (always runs in finally)

Implementation lives under tests/e2e/flows/, tests/e2e/provisioners/, and tests/e2e/verifiers/.

docs.title: Tier commands
docs.text:
• Fast required: python -m pytest -q -m "tier_fast and not quarantined" --maxfail=1 --no-cov
  • Heavy optional: python -m pytest -q -m "tier_heavy and not tier_external" --maxfail=1 --durations=25
  • External nightly/release: python -m pytest -q -m "tier_external and cleanup_required" --maxfail=1 --durations=50

docs.title: Environment model
docs.text:
Common:

  • TESTO_E2E_RUN_ID (optional; auto-generated if not set)
  • TESTO_E2E_KEEP_ON_FAIL (default false)
  • TESTO_E2E_MAX_CLEANUP_ATTEMPTS (default 3)
  • TESTO_E2E_EXTERNAL_DRY_RUN (true by default; set false in external CI gates)

GitHub external:

  • TESTO_E2E_GITHUB_TOKEN
  • TESTO_E2E_GITHUB_OWNER

GitLab external:

  • TESTO_E2E_GITLAB_TOKEN
  • TESTO_E2E_GITLAB_GROUP_ID
  • TESTO_E2E_GITLAB_BASE_URL (optional, defaults to https://gitlab.com/api/v4)

docs.title: Isolation and naming
docs.text:
• Ephemeral resources are named using testo-e2e-<run-id>-<provider>-<scenario>.
  • Artifacts are written under .artifacts/e2e/<run-id>/.
  • External CI jobs use external-e2e concurrency/resource locking.

docs.title: Cleanup guarantees
docs.text:
• Every scenario writes cleanup records through cleanup_ledger.
  • Session finalizer emits .artifacts/e2e/<run-id>/cleanup-ledger.json.
  • External gates fail if cleanup audit detects any cleanup_failed record.

docs.title: Diagnostics artifacts
docs.text:
On failed heavy/external runs, upload:

  • logs (*.log)
  • summary JSON (*summary*.json)
  • API responses (*api*.json)
  • screenshots (*.png, if UI scenarios are enabled)

docs.title: Security and redaction
docs.text:
• Provider tokens must be injected via masked CI secrets/variables only.
  • Do not print or serialize tokens into logs/artifacts.
  • Keep provider API logic inside tests/e2e/provisioners/ adapters.

Context & Links: - QA Strategies § Testing the orchestrator itself, Technical Debt Tracker, CI-CD Pipeline Setup

docs.title: GitLab Pages Demo
docs.text:
A public, link-shareable demo of Testo: a CI pipeline runs real testo run cycles, then publishes the React UI to a static Pages site showing the results of those runs. The same pipeline exists twice:

  • GitHub Pages (.github/workflows/pages-demo.yml) at https://taltal-beep.github.io/testosterone/. This is the main demo link; see GitHub Pages.
  • GitLab Pages (.gitlab-ci.yml), for showing the same thing on GitLab; see What you have to do on GitLab.

It runs two things:

  • Testosterone testing itself: its own fast Python suite, split into a unit and an integration/contract stage so the dashboard's pyramid is real.
  • fake-api, a deliberately silly app ("Fake Doing Bullshit") with a flaky route, a broken route and a slow route. Its tests describe how the app should behave, so the broken parts fail them honestly. Nothing in the tests is rigged.

Green-only data proves little about a test tool, which is why the second target exists: it guarantees failures, flakiness and slowness to look at, and every one of them traces back to a line of app code.

Live site: https://<namespace>.gitlab.io/<project>/ (see What you have to do on GitLab).

Related: CI-CD Pipeline Setup (the reusable template for running Testo in your pipeline), Architecture Overview.

docs.title: Why it is built this way
docs.text:
GitLab Pages serves static files only, so it cannot host testo_api (FastAPI). Publishing the UI therefore needs run data frozen into files.

What it does not do is reimplement the UI against fixtures. Instead:

  1. scripts/export_static_site.py calls every read-only endpoint the UI uses — in-process, through TestClient against the same create_app() the real server runs — and writes each response body to a JSON file.
  2. frontend/src/lib/static-backend.ts installs a fetch shim in builds made with VITE_STATIC_DATA_BASE, mapping each API request onto the file the export wrote for it.

The pages, the API client and the query layer are unchanged, so the published dashboard renders the same payloads the live API produces. The cost of the trick is a layout contract between those two files, pinned by tests/unit/ci/test_gitlab_pages_demo_contract.py.

testo run (self-test, fake-api)
  └─ history DB + static/history/<run_id>/ (Allure HTML)
       └─ export_static_site.py ──► public/data/**.json  +  public/history/**
                                        └─ vite build ──► public/  ──► GitLab Pages
                                             (static-backend.ts reads data/)

docs.title: What the pipeline runs
docs.text:
.gitlab-ci.yml at the repo root (the reusable customer-facing template stays in ci/gitlab/testo.gitlab-ci.yml):

Job Stage What it does run_demo_cycles demo Installs the package and Playwright's Chromium, clones fake-api into .demo/fake-api, runs self-test and fake-api once each, exports the site into public/. pages deploy Builds the frontend in static mode and copies it over public/, then copies index.html to 404.html so deep links survive a refresh.

Both cycles live in the root testosterone.yaml:

Cycle Stages (tier) Expected result self-test core-unit (unit), core-integration (integration) Green. A red self-test fails the pipeline and nothing is published. fake-api unit (unit), api (integration), buttons Behave (integration), ui Playwright (e2e) Red by design: broken and slow always fail, flaky fails about a third of the time.

Each pipeline runs fake-api once. The cached history (below) holds the previous pipelines' runs, so Compare puts this run next to the last one and shows which tests changed, such as the flaky route passing in one pipeline and failing in the next. The very first pipeline has nothing to compare against yet.

Run history goes to file-backed SQLite inside the job workspace (DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.ci-history/testo.db), so the demo needs no database service and no credentials. The DB and the Allure HTML under static/history/ are kept in a GitLab cache between pipelines (the 20 newest report trees are kept), so the trend grows with every pipeline. The cache is best-effort: if GitLab drops it, the next pipeline starts a fresh history.

The self-test's nested pytest gets DATABASE_URL=sqlite:////tmp/testo-self-test.db through extra_env, so testosterone's own tests never write into the history of the run that is executing them.

docs.title: Build-time variables the pages job sets
docs.text:
Variable Value Why VITE_BASE Pages subpath, e.g. /testosterone/ Vite asset URLs and the router basename. VITE_STATIC_DATA_BASE <subpath>/data Where the shim reads the exported JSON. VITE_API_BASE_URL $CI_PAGES_URL Report links render as <API base>/history/…, which on Pages is the published copy of static/history/.

All three are derived from CI_PAGES_URL; nothing is hardcoded, so the same pipeline works for project, user and group Pages.

docs.title: Running it locally
docs.text:
pip install -e ".[dev]"
npm install                       # Allure 3 CLI, for the HTML reports
git clone https://github.com/taltal-beep/fake-api.git .demo/fake-api
pip install -r .demo/fake-api/requirements.txt
python -m playwright install chromium

testo run --cycle self-test --ci
testo run --cycle fake-api --ci || true
testo run --cycle fake-api --ci || true   # a second run gives Compare a pair locally
python scripts/export_static_site.py --out public --site-url http://localhost:8090/testo --demo-resources

cd frontend
VITE_BASE=/testo/ VITE_STATIC_DATA_BASE=/testo/data \
  VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8090/testo npm run build
cd .. && cp -r frontend/dist/. public/ && cp public/index.html public/404.html

--demo-resources fills the throwaway history database with the made-up pools from testo lease demo first, so the Resources page has something to show. Leave it off when exporting a real database.

Serve public/ under a /testo/ path (any static server) and the demo behaves as it does on Pages, except for the 404 fallback, which is Pages-specific.

docs.title: What visitors see
docs.text:
A dismissible notice above the header marks the build read-only, says what the two cycles are (testosterone testing itself, and fake-api, whose red is deliberate) and links to the pipeline that produced it. Its × button closes it and the choice is remembered in localStorage (testo.demoNotice.dismissed); a "Read-only demo" badge in the header stays visible and toggles the notice (frontend/src/components/StaticBuildBanner.tsx). Writes have nothing behind them, so the shim answers them with 405 read_only_build ("This is a read-only demo snapshot…"). The NDJSON event stream is likewise absent: a static host cannot stream a run that is not running.

  • Cycles page: only cycles with a run in the snapshot are exported, so every card leads to real history. Run buttons (on the cards and the cycle page) are disabled and show the local command instead (testo run --cycle <name>).
  • AI Failure Summary: a visitor's click cannot reach an AI provider, so the export generates the summary for each failed run beforehand, through the same POST /runs/{id}/ai-summary:generate the button calls, and the Run detail page shows that frozen summary (the button itself is disabled). This needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the export step's environment (see Optional: AI summaries); without it the card says summaries are generated live when you run Testosterone locally.

Report links work: static/history/<run_id>/ is copied into the published site, so the Allure reports for each framework open from the Run detail page.

docs.title: Optional: AI summaries
docs.text:
scripts/export_static_site.py freezes one AI failure summary per failed run when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set. The model defaults to claude-haiku-4-5 (override with TESTO_DEMO_AI_MODEL). A generated summary is stored with the run in the cached history DB, so later pipelines reuse it; a failed attempt is retried on the next pipeline. Each request gets one 30-second attempt, and an error only skips that summary, never the deploy. The key is only read from the environment; it is never written to the site.

  • GitHub: add a repository secret named ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; the export step passes ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }} through. Unset, it is empty and the export skips the summaries.
  • GitLab: add a masked CI/CD variable named ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

docs.title: GitHub Pages
docs.text:
.github/workflows/pages-demo.yml has the same steps as the GitLab job, in one build job and a deploy job:

Trigger What happens Push to main, nightly schedule, manual run Build, then deploy to Pages. Pull request touching the demo files Build only, so a broken demo fails the PR instead of the site.

The same site also carries the docs: the build job runs mkdocs build --strict --site-dir public/docs, so the vault is at https://taltal-beep.github.io/testosterone/docs/ (Docs Site). Pull requests that touch mkdocs.yml or scripts/mkdocs_hooks.py build it too.

Run history is restored from and saved to the Actions cache under a fresh key per run (testo-demo-history-<run_id>, restored by prefix), because Actions caches cannot be overwritten. Only the deploy job gets pages: write.

One-time setup: Settings → Pages → Source → GitHub Actions. The first deployment happens on the next push to main (or Actions → Pages demo → Run workflow); the URL then also shows on the workflow run and under Settings → Pages.

docs.title: What you have to do on GitLab
docs.text:
Everything above is in the repository; these steps need a human and a GitLab account.

  1. Create the GitLab project, e.g. gitlab.com/<user>/testosterone, public (Pages sites on GitLab.com are public unless Pages Access Control is enabled; a private project's site is visible only to members).
  2. Get the code there. GitLab's pull mirroring (GitLab fetches from GitHub) is a Premium feature, so on Free use one of:
  3. the included .github/workflows/mirror-to-gitlab.yml, which pushes main to GitLab on every push. Set repository variable GITLAB_MIRROR_URL and secret GITLAB_MIRROR_TOKEN (a GitLab project access token with write_repository) on GitHub; the workflow is inert until both exist;
  4. or a one-off git push to a second remote.
  5. Check runners. GitLab.com shared runners need an account with CI/CD minutes available; GitLab.com asks free-tier accounts to complete identity verification (a payment method on file) before shared runners pick up jobs. A self-hosted runner works too.
  6. Run the pipeline — it runs on pushes to the default branch, and can be started from CI/CD → Pipelines → Run pipeline.
  7. Open the site at Deploy → Pages, which shows the URL (https://<namespace>.gitlab.io/<project>/). The first deployment can take a few minutes to become reachable.

Nothing in the pipeline needs secrets; the only credentials anywhere are the mirror token in step 2, if you choose that route, and the optional AI key (see Optional: AI summaries).

docs.title: Maintenance notes
docs.text:
• FAKE_API_REPO / FAKE_API_REF in .gitlab-ci.yml choose what is cloned; pin FAKE_API_REF to a tag to freeze the demo.
  • tests/unit/ci/test_gitlab_pages_demo_contract.py asserts the cycles exist, that the fake-api cycle points where the pipeline clones it, and that only fake-api is allowed to fail.
  • Compare's Test-Level Changes needs each run's own copy of its per-test results under static/history/<run_id>/artifacts/ (PR #68). That folder is in the history cache, and the prune step trims it with the reports.
  • Adding a UI page that calls a new endpoint means exporting it in scripts/export_static_site.py and mapping it in static-backend.ts, otherwise the demo shows that panel's error state.
  • The export scrubs checkout-absolute paths out of the payloads before they are published.

docs.title: Publishing Docker Images
docs.text: Index · Publishing to PyPI · Publishing to Artifactory

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Three images are published to GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) via GitHub Actions, from one matrix job in docker-publish.yml: testo-runner (Dockerfile.testo-runner, the CLI for running cycles in CI, and the default image stages run in with TESTO_RUNNER=container), testo-server (Dockerfile.testo-server, the API with the web UI built in, used by the Team Server) and testo-runner-service (Dockerfile.testo-runner-service, the service that starts each stage in a throwaway container, Runs in throwaway containers). Images are built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 on the floating python:3.11-slim-bookworm base, so each build picks up current Debian security fixes, and are scanned with Trivy before they are pushed.

docs.title: Registry
docs.text:
• Registry: ghcr.io
  • Images: ghcr.io/taltal-beep/testo-runner, ghcr.io/taltal-beep/testo-server, ghcr.io/taltal-beep/testo-runner-service
  • Auth: Uses GITHUB_TOKEN (automatic for public repos, no additional secrets needed)
