docs.title: Context
docs.text: On a pull request most of a suite tests code the change didn't touch. Running only the tests a change can affect makes CI faster, but a selection that misses a test hides a failure until main breaks. Taltal asked for it (2026-10-30) with three conditions: map changes to tests from past coverage or configurable path-to-test globs, fall back to running everything when unsure, and show why each test was picked. Off by default.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
testo_core/services/affected_tests.py picks the tests; two opt-in entry points use it:

  • testo affected prints the tests and the reason for each (text, --json, or --list for other runners' command lines).
  • pytest --testo-affected (or TESTO_AFFECTED=1) deselects the rest inside pytest, so pytest users need no script. It runs before --testo-shard, so shards split only the affected tests.

Changed files are the working tree against the merge base with the baseline branch, plus untracked files (so a local run sees uncommitted work). git diff --no-renames lists both names of a moved file. The base is --base, else affected.base, else the pull request's target branch from the CI variables testo_core/services/ci_provenance.py already reads, else origin/main.

Mapping, for each changed file, first match wins (affected: in testosterone.yaml, parsed by testo_core/config/affected.py):

Step Source Result 1 run_all_when (built in: conftest.py, pyproject.toml, lockfiles, testosterone.yaml, ...) run everything 2 ignore (built in: __pycache__/, *.pyc, .pytest_cache/, ...) no test 3 test_files name patterns (test_*.py, *.spec.ts, *_test.go, ...) that file; nothing if it was deleted 4 rules: changed globs to tests globs or pytest node ids those tests 5 a coverage.py JSON report with test contexts (pytest --cov --cov-context=test, coverage json --show-contexts) the tests that ran a line of the file

When unsure, run everything. A file no step maps, a file the coverage report lists but no test ran (only imported), a rule whose test globs match no file, a failed git diff, an unknown base and an empty diff each add a reason to run_all_reasons, and any reason means the whole suite. In pytest, a picked Python test that wasn't collected (renamed since the coverage report, or outside the paths pytest was given) also runs everything. Only ignore can make a change run nothing; pytest then exits 0 instead of its "no tests ran" 5.

Why each test. Every picked test carries "<changed file>: <why>" lines; testo affected prints them, --json returns them, and pytest prints the first 20 in its summary.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Nothing changes unless a user passes --testo-affected or calls testo affected. testo run doesn't select by itself: a stage's command line belongs to the user, and --list gives them the tests to put in it.
  • Run history isn't a mapping source: a run records outcomes, not which files a test touched. Coverage contexts are the "past" signal, and they go stale; the run-all fallbacks (a test that isn't collected, a file the report doesn't list) catch the common cases, and a periodic full run (nightly, or on main) catches the rest.
  • Coverage is pytest-only for now (contexts are pytest node ids). Other runners use rules and changed test files.
  • Reference: Command Reference § testo affected.

docs.title: Alerts Where Developers Look - 2026-10-22
docs.text: Part of the mainstream-adoption work (Specs & ADRs).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A run's results reached people in two places: the dashboard, which someone has to remember to open, and the job summary / pull request comment from the GitHub Action. Tools teams adopt also post to chat, mark failures on the diff, and file flaky tests as work. The testbeats reporter already posted to Slack and Teams, but only counts, on every run, with no failing test names and nothing about what changed.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• One message, built from run history. testo_core/services/run_alerts.py builds the alert from the same RunSummary as testo report markdown (failing tests, per-test changes since the previous run) plus newly_flaky_tests(). It lists new regressions, newly flaky tests, failing tests and fixes, 10 names each. Any recorded run can be sent again.
  • Two entry points, same code. slack and teams reporters send it right after testo run (reporters run after the run is recorded, so context.run_id is set). testo notify --to slack|teams sends it later, which is what the GitHub Action and any other CI call. testbeats stays as it was.
  • Quiet by default. when: failure sends only for a red run or a newly flaky test; change sends when the result flipped or a test regressed, got fixed or became flaky; always sends every run.
  • "Newly flaky" means this run made it flaky: flaky in the window ending at the run and not in the window ending at the run before. A flaky test is announced once, not on every run.
  • Webhook URLs are secrets. They come from TESTO_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL / TESTO_TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL or a ${env:…} reporter option, never a CLI flag, and errors never include them. The action takes them as slack-webhook / teams-webhook inputs fed from repository secrets.
  • Annotations use workflow commands, not the Checks API. testo report annotations prints ::error file=…,line=…:: lines; GitHub attaches them to the job's check run and shows them on the diff. That needs no token or permission and works on fork pull requests, so the action does it by default. The line is the first stack-trace frame inside the workspace (pytest path:line: and Python File "…", line N frames), tried against each stage's target_repo because runners print paths relative to it. GitHub keeps 10 error annotations per step, so the rest are counted in one notice.
  • Flaky issues are opt-in action code. flaky-issues: "true" reads testo flaky --new --json and opens one issue per test, titled Flaky test: <name> (<cycle>) and labelled flaky-test, skipping titles that already have an open issue. It needs issues: write, so it is off by default. Like the comment, it is standard library urllib and never changes the step's exit code.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Alerts, "newly flaky" and "since the previous run" need history from earlier runs; in CI that means a cached or shared database, the same as the PR comment.
  • Annotations only land on a line when the runner writes a stack trace into the Allure results (pytest, Behave). Others are still annotated, just without a file.
  • Usage: Command Reference § testo notify, CI-CD Pipeline Setup.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Before this batch the CLI and the API ran cycles through two different code paths, the frontend's API types were written by hand, run history was read through several ad-hoc helpers, and mypy and ruff format were advisory. The project is meant to be read by other engineers, so the structure had to be explainable in one diagram.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Change Pull request Accurate ARCHITECTURE.md with a system diagram; frontend CI job; generated artifacts untracked #61 The cycle use case moves into services/cycle_run.CycleRunService, shared by CLI and API #60 The legacy execution stack is retired; every run goes through the cycle engine #62 Frontend API types are generated from FastAPI's OpenAPI schema and typechecked in CI #63 One storage boundary for run history (testo_core/history/) #65 mypy backlog cleared; mypy and ruff format are blocking in CI #64 changelog-on-main skips instead of failing when bot secrets are missing #66

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One engine: config/loader.py → config/resolver.py → engine/orchestrator.run_plan() → engine/executor.run_stage(), entered only through CycleRunService. See Architecture Overview.
  • A backend schema change that the frontend doesn't regenerate for fails CI.
  • The 2026-10-07 Interview Readiness Fixes build on this base.

docs.title: Architecture Review - 2026-10-31
docs.text:
Specs & ADRs · Architecture Overview · Project Review

A structural review of the codebase at 8a78225 (1.5.0), done with the Claude Fable 5.1 model and the architecture review skill. It looks at module boundaries, layering, coupling, the data model and its migrations, scaling limits and extension points, and compares them with what ARCHITECTURE.md and the diagrams claim. The Project Review scores the whole repo; this note only ranks the architecture's pressure points and recommends what to do about each. It proposes; nothing here was built.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
The architecture is sound for what the project is today: one engine entered through CycleRunService, typed events as the seam between engine and renderers, adapters behind a small protocol, entry-point plugins, generated frontend types. Every feature shipped in October (ingest, team server, quarantine, triage, pools, container runner, OTel) landed without a second path, which is the best evidence the shape works.

The pressure points are all on the read side, not the engine. Run history is one table with a JSON blob, per-test data lives in files on disk, and most analytics load the last 500 runs into Python and filter there. That is fine for a laptop and a small team server, and it is the first thing that will break when a team points many CI jobs at one server. The second theme is that ARCHITECTURE.md has drifted from the code in a few places (session boundary, services/ as "analytics", "sequential stages"), and nothing in CI stops layering from drifting further.

docs.title: Ranked findings
docs.text: Ranking is by how much a future change would cost if the finding is left alone. Severity is High when it limits a documented use (team server), Medium when it costs maintainers time, Low when it is cosmetic drift.

docs.title: R1. Per-test data is files, not rows (High)
docs.text:
Per-test outcomes, durations and flaky signals come from each run's Allure *-result.json copied to static/history/<run_id>/artifacts/ (persistence/db_backend.py, _snapshot_run_artifacts). flaky_service, test_history, run_failures, project_health, run_summary_markdown and otel_export each call list_recent_runs(limit=500), filter the cycle in Python (8 such sites) and then open files per run.

Consequences today:

  • The API must share a disk with every run it shows. The team server does (ingest writes locally), so it works, but the design can never put the API behind a load balancer or move artifacts to object storage without rewriting every analytics module.
  • Every per-test request is O(runs × tests) file reads; the per-test page, Compare and /health re-parse the same JSON on every call. There is no cache.
  • A cycle with more than 500 runs silently loses history: _SCAN_LIMIT = 500 is a hard ceiling in five modules.
  • Disk grows without bound. static/history/ has no retention; testo clean removes artifacts/, not history.

docs.title: R2. One table, one JSON column (High)
docs.text:
RunRecord has id, status, start_time, end_time and metadata (JSON). The cycle name, health, exit code, branch, commit, stages and the snapshot pointer are all inside the blob. There is no index on start_time, no cycle column, and the repository protocol has one list method (list_recent_runs) and one status filter. Every "runs of cycle X" and every dashboard rollup is a full scan of the newest N rows plus JSON decoding in Python.

This also makes the data model unqueryable from outside Testosterone (SQL dashboards, Grafana), which teams running Postgres will ask for.

docs.title: R3. No migrations (Medium, becomes High at the next schema change)
docs.text: Schema is SQLModel.metadata.create_all() on startup (repository/db_config.py). ReportArchive's docstring already says existing deployments "need a manual ALTER TABLE". Ten tables now exist (runs, archives, queue, users, audit, triage, four resource tables), the team server runs Postgres, and the first column added to any of them after 1.5.0 will break upgrades for everyone on a persistent database. Fixing R1 or R2 requires this first.

docs.title: R4. services/ is the catch-all (Medium)
docs.text: testo_core/services/ is 32 modules and about 7,000 lines, the largest package in the repo. It holds the use case (cycle_run), analytics (delta, flaky, dashboard, test history), write paths (junit_ingest, triage, report_archive), exporters (otel_export, run_summary_markdown, badge), the AI subsystem, and two review features (project_health, project_review). ARCHITECTURE.md describes it as "Analytics". New code has nowhere else obvious to go, so it goes here.

docs.title: R5. The session boundary moved and nobody told the docs (Medium)
docs.text: ARCHITECTURE.md says testo_core/repository/ is "the only code that opens a database session". Four other modules now open Session(engine) directly: accounts.py, services/triage.py, resources/store.py and testo_api/run_queue.py. Each is tidy on its own, but there are now five places that must agree on dialect quirks, retries and testing doubles, and the rule that made the storage layer explainable in one sentence is gone. Either the rule is reinstated or the docs should say "one engine factory, several stores".

docs.title: R6. Nothing enforces layering (Medium)
docs.text:
The dependency direction is mostly right (nothing in services/, engine/ or reporting/ imports cli/; testo_core imports testo_api only in cli/commands/ui_cmd.py, which is the deliberate testo ui entry). But there are small inversions that will multiply without a check:

  • engine/ and config/ import reporting.paths for safe_child_path and plan_artifacts_dir, which are path helpers, not reporting.
  • config/ imports resources.pools (three modules) and reporting; the configuration layer now depends on two feature packages.
  • persistence/ imports engine, reporting, repository and security.

None of this is wrong in isolation, but the layer table in ARCHITECTURE.md is a promise that CI does not keep. An import-linter contract (about 20 lines of config) would.

docs.title: R7. In-process state limits the API to one process (Medium, documented)
docs.text: CycleExecutionManager, the login throttle, the AI settings store (file-backed, but cached per process) and the SSE file tail all assume one uvicorn worker. TESTO_RUN_QUEUE=db makes queued runs survive a restart, but a second API process would still double-start cycles and see different live state. This is written down in "Trade-offs and known limits" and is acceptable for the stated audience. It is listed here because R1 to R3 and R7 are the same decision: whether the team server is ever meant to scale past one box.

docs.title: R8. Plugin API has no version (Low)
docs.text: FrameworkAdapter and BaseReporter are the public extension points, loaded by entry points. Neither carries an API version, and testo plugins cannot tell a plugin built for 1.3 from one built for 1.5. Adding a method to FrameworkAdapter (as native_report already was) breaks third-party adapters at call time, not load time.

docs.title: R9. Concurrency model for parallel stages is per-process (Low)
docs.text: With max_parallel_stages, several stages append to one events.ndjson from threads in one process. That is safe with the GIL and line-sized writes, but the format has no sequence number, so a consumer cannot order or de-duplicate events once a run is spread over the container runner service or two processes. A seq field on every event is cheap now and impossible to retrofit later.

docs.title: R10. Documentation drift (Low)
docs.text: Besides R5: the layer table still says run_plan() runs stages "in order" (parallel stages exist), lists services/ as analytics only, and the test layout note (tests/TEST_LAYOUT.md) describes a migration that finished long ago and a tests/contracts/ folder with one file next to tests/contract/ with 26. Small, but the vault's rule is "docs stay in sync", and these are the notes an outside contributor reads first.

docs.title: What is good and should not change
docs.text:
• One engine, one use case. CycleRunService is still the only caller of run_plan(); the CLI, the API, ingest, pytest --testo and the Action all go through it.
  • Events as the seam. Typed events, NDJSON on disk, renderers decide presentation. The container runner backend slotted in under the executor without touching the engine's contract, which is the proof the seam is in the right place.
  • Backends behind a protocol (engine/backends/, StageProcess), so the host and container runners are interchangeable and the API never sees a Docker socket.
  • Generated frontend types with a CI gate on drift. 85 Pydantic models in one testo_api/models.py is big but it is one place, and that is the point.
  • Switchable team features default off (TESTO_AUTH, TESTO_RUN_QUEUE, TESTO_RUNNER, TESTO_REPORTS_ORIGIN): a solo user's install stays simple.
  • Exit codes single-sourced and locked by contract tests.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text: Ordered by value for effort. The first three are one decision in three steps; the rest are independent.

docs.title: 1. Add migrations before anything else touches the schema
docs.text:
Decision: introduce Alembic with a baseline revision equal to today's create_all() schema; testo-api and testo config-db run upgrade head on startup, SQLite included. Keep create_all() only for the in-memory test database.

Option Complexity Risk Notes A. Alembic, autogenerate from SQLModel metadata Low Low Standard, one dependency already pulled in by SQLAlchemy's ecosystem. Recommended. B. Hand-rolled schema_version table plus ALTER scripts Low Medium Reinvents Alembic, three dialects to test by hand. C. Keep create_all(), document "drop and recreate" None High Unacceptable once the team server has a Postgres with months of history.

Consequences: every later schema change (2, 3 below) is a revision; the docker-compose team server upgrades in place; the Repository Pattern ADR gets a section on migrations. About one PR.

docs.title: 2. Promote the hot columns out of the JSON blob
docs.text:
Decision: add real columns to RunRecord for cycle, health_pct, exit_code, branch, commit, source and snapshot_dir, with indexes on (cycle, start_time) and start_time. Keep metadata for everything else. Add list_runs(cycle=..., since=..., limit=...) to the repository protocol and move the eight Python-side cycle filters onto it.

Option Complexity Scalability Notes A. Columns + indexes, blob stays for the long tail Medium Good Dialect-portable, SQL-queryable from Grafana. Recommended. B. Dialect JSON indexes (JSONB GIN on Postgres, json_extract on SQLite) Medium Medium Three dialects, three syntaxes, MySQL weakest; the blob stays the contract. C. Leave as is, raise _SCAN_LIMIT None Poor Pushes the cliff back, keeps O(N) decoding per request.

Consequences: _SCAN_LIMIT disappears; the dashboard and cycle pages stop reading JSON they do not need; history/views.py becomes a thin mapper. Needs 1. One or two PRs.

docs.title: 3. Give tests a table
docs.text:
Decision: on each run, write one row per test case (run_id, stage, key, status, duration_ms, message truncated) into a test_result table from the same Allure JSON the snapshot already parses. Flaky, per-test history, "got slower", triage and /health read the table; the files stay for attachments, traces and the Compare download.

Option Complexity Scalability Notes A. test_result table written by DbBackend, files kept for artifacts Medium-High Good The API no longer needs the run's disk for analytics; retention becomes a DELETE. Recommended. B. Cache parsed snapshots in memory per process Low Medium Helps latency, not the disk coupling or the 500-run ceiling. C. Move snapshots to object storage, keep file reads High Medium Solves disk sharing, keeps O(runs × tests) parsing.

Consequences: the biggest change in this note and the one that makes the team server honest about scale. Each analytics module shrinks (they already share _load_cases). Suites with tens of thousands of tests per run produce large tables; message must be bounded and old rows pruned (see 6). Two or three PRs, behind nothing (it is a write-side addition; reads can switch one module at a time). Needs 1 and 2.

docs.title: 4. Enforce the layer table with import-linter
docs.text: Add an importlinter config to pyproject.toml with three contracts: testo_core must not import testo_api except cli/commands/ui_cmd.py; engine, config, frameworks, paths must not import services, reporting, cli, resources; persistence and history may import repository but not each other. Run it in the format CI job. Move safe_child_path and plan_artifacts_dir from reporting/paths.py into testo_core/paths.py to make the first contract pass. Half a day, and it stops R6 from growing.

docs.title: 5. Split services/ by role
docs.text: Not a rewrite: three moves and a docstring. services/cycle_run.py is the use case and stays. Analytics (delta_*, flaky_service, test_history, dashboard_service, attention, run_failures, run_snapshot_diff, project_health) become testo_core/analytics/. Exporters (otel_export, run_summary_markdown, badge, report_archive*) join reporting/. Write paths (junit_ingest, triage, run_annotations, test_ownership) stay in services/. services/ai/ stays. Then the layer table in ARCHITECTURE.md can name each package in one line. One mechanical PR per move; import-linter from 4 keeps them apart afterwards.

docs.title: 6. Retention for static/history/
docs.text: A history.retention config key (days and/or runs per cycle) and a testo clean --history command that deletes the oldest rows and their static/history/<run_id>/ directories together, run by the API on a timer when set. Without it the team server's disk is the real _SCAN_LIMIT. Small, independent of 1 to 3.

docs.title: 7. Version the plugin API
docs.text: Add TESTO_PLUGIN_API = 1 in testo_core/plugins.py, let an adapter or reporter class declare plugin_api = 1, and have testo plugins and load_framework() warn on a mismatch. Document in Plugin API which protocol methods are optional. One small PR; it makes native_report-style additions safe.

docs.title: 8. Add seq to engine events
docs.text: An integer sequence per run in engine/events.py, written to events.ndjson and forwarded by SSE and the container runner. The frontend can then de-duplicate reconnects and the OTel exporter can order spans without the wall clock. Tiny, and only cheap now.

docs.title: 9. Fix the doc drift in one PR
docs.text: ARCHITECTURE.md: the session rule (R5), services/ description (R4), "in order" (R10), and a "Scaling" subsection that says plainly: one API process, shared disk, SQLite or Postgres, and what 1 to 3 would change. Retire tests/TEST_LAYOUT.md's migration map into docs/Archive/ and fold the tier list into tests/README.md. Half a day.

docs.title: Not recommended
docs.text:
• Microservices or a message broker. The in-process worker pool plus TESTO_RUN_QUEUE=db is the right size; the container runner service is already the one process boundary that security needs.
  • Replacing SQLModel. The three-dialect story works; the problem is the shape of one table, not the ORM.
  • A second UI or a plugin UI slot. Not asked for, and the generated-types gate is worth more than extensibility here.

docs.title: Sequence
docs.text:
1. Migrations (rec. 1), import-linter and path helper move (rec. 4), doc drift (rec. 9), event seq (rec. 8). All small, no behaviour change.
  2. Hot columns and the repository query (rec. 2), retention (rec. 6).
  3. test_result table and switching analytics onto it (rec. 3), then the services/ split (rec. 5) once the analytics modules have shrunk.
  4. Plugin API version (rec. 7) in the release after, so plugin authors get one notice.

Nothing above changes testosterone.yaml, the CLI contract or exit codes. Recommendations 2 and 3 change the database schema and need 1 first.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Architecture Consolidation - 2026-10-06: the decisions this review builds on.
  • Repository Pattern - Database-Agnostic Refactor: where recommendations 1 to 3 would be recorded once decided.
  • Scale Runs and Stages - 2026-10-24 and Switchable Team Features - 2026-10-24: the write-side scaling work already done.
  • Throwaway Stage Containers - 2026-10-24: the backend seam praised above.
  • Technical Debt Tracker: the open items R1 to R10 should be mirrored into once Taltal picks which to do.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
A BehaveX stage should leave two things: BehaveX's own HTML report (the stage's native report, behave_reports/report.html) and Allure results (allure-results/behavex/) for summaries, health and every reporter.

The adapter used to get the Allure results by passing BehaveX's --formatter=...:AllureBehaveXFormatter. BehaveX skips report.html whenever a formatter is set (behavex.utils.generate_reports), so BehaveX never wrote it. A post-stage hook re-rendered it from report.json inside Testo's process, but with the formatter on, BehaveX put scenario logs in the Allure folder, so the re-rendered report had no scenario logs.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. BehaveXAdapter.build_argv passes no formatter. BehaveX writes report.html, report.json and outputs/logs/ to behave_reports/ as it does on its own.
  2. After the stage, the executor calls export_behavex_allure_results (testo_core/reporting/behavex_allure.py). It copies the scenario logs into allure-results/behavex/ and runs BehaveX's own AllureBehaveXFormatter on report.json, with BehaveX's logs setting pointed there. The output is the same set of files a --formatter run writes, with scenario.log attachments that resolve.
  3. A --formatter in a stage's args is passed through. The export then sees existing results and does nothing, and ensure_behavex_report_html still renders report.html from report.json, as before.
  4. Both steps are best-effort: a failure goes to run.log and StageResult.error; the exit code still decides the stage.

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
• Keep the formatter and only re-render the HTML afterwards (the old behaviour). Rejected: the HTML loses scenario logs and the native report depends on Testo rebuilding it from BehaveX internals.
  • Run the formatter as a subprocess (python -m behavex.outputs.formatters.allure_behavex_formatter). Rejected: its command line has no output directory option, so it writes to ./output/allure-results.
  • Write our own report.json → Allure converter. Rejected: BehaveX already ships one, and reusing it keeps attachments, labels and categories identical to a --formatter run.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Allure results for a BehaveX stage appear when the stage ends, not while it runs. Reporters run after the whole cycle, so they still see every result.
  • Scenario logs are stored twice (in behave_reports/outputs/logs/ and in allure-results/behavex/). They are small text files.
  • tests/integration/testo_core/engine/test_behavex_reports.py runs the real behavex binary and fails if either report is missing or the HTML is not BehaveX's own.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The first external adopter, CarBiz (an Expo app with a Python/AWS backend), wants one orchestrated run across pytest suites, Jest, Playwright and, later, Maestro. Before this change Testo only ran pytest, Behave and BehaveX. Any other runner could not be a stage, and even a wrapper script would produce no Allure results, so it counted as an empty stage in summaries and health %.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. New equipment command (testo_core/frameworks/command_adapter.py). args is the complete argv, run verbatim in target_repo. Nothing is injected (these runners have no Allure flag). TESTO_SHARED_ALLURE_RESULTS_DIR is still exported for runners that can write Allure JSON themselves. args is required at load time. The default tier is unit; set tier: explicitly for e2e suites.
  2. New stage key junit_xml (string or list of globs, relative to target_repo, valid on every equipment). After the process exits, the executor converts each matching file into one Allure *-result.json per <testcase> (testo_core/reporting/junit_import.py):
  3. Status: <failure> → failed, <error> → broken, <skipped> → skipped, otherwise passed.
  4. statusDetails carries the message and a trace capped at 20k characters.
  5. historyId = sha256(stage name + full name), so trends line up across runs.
  6. Timing comes from the suite timestamp plus the per-case time, laid out sequentially.
  7. Safety.
  8. Patterns must be relative and cannot use ... Matches that resolve outside target_repo (for example symlinks) are skipped.
  9. Files older than the stage start are ignored, so a stale report never masquerades as this run.
  10. Parsing uses stdlib expat, which does not resolve external entities.
  11. The import is best-effort, like the BehaveX report hook: the exit code still decides pass/fail, and the outcome is appended to run.log.

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
• Copy the JUnit XML into allure-results/ and let Allure read it. Rejected. Allure's HTML would show the tests, but allure_results.parse_collected_results only reads *-result.json, so summaries, health %, the DB archive and the dashboard would still see an empty stage.
  • A dedicated adapter per tool (Jest, Playwright, ...). Deferred. Every one of them already emits JUnit, so one generic path covers them all. Per-tool adapters only make sense for native report bundles (native_report), which can be added later without changing this contract.
  • Fail the stage when the report is missing. Rejected. A crashed runner already exits non-zero, and a passing run with a misconfigured glob should be visible (the run.log line) without masking the real result.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• SUPPORTED_FRAMEWORKS gains command, and Stage gains junit_xml (default (), so existing configs are unchanged).
  • Docs updated in the same change: Architecture Overview (adapter list), Deep Dive - Execution Logic (post-stage hook), QA Strategies (config example), CHANGELOG.md.
  • Tests: tests/unit/testo_core/test_command_adapter.py, 14 cases covering config validation, the adapter, the status and label mapping, malformed, stale and escaping files, and real subprocess stages through run_stage.

docs.title: Follow-ups
docs.text:
• Coverage aggregation per cycle (fail_under) and flaky-test tracking, which the CarBiz pilot needs next (see the CarBiz vault note "Test Strategy - 2026-09-25").
  • A Maestro example cycle once CarBiz's native flows exist.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: testosterone.yaml had no JSON Schema, so editors could not suggest its keys or flag a typo such as worker: until testo config validate ran. Most YAML-driven tools ship one; editors with a YAML language server (VS Code's Red Hat YAML extension, JetBrains, Neovim) load it from a URL or a # yaml-language-server: $schema=... line.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. testo_core/config/json_schema.py builds a draft-07 schema from the constants in testo_core/config/schema.py (SUPPORTED_FRAMEWORKS, SUPPORTED_TIERS, SUPPORTED_REPORTER_TYPES, Defaults). The loader stays the source of truth for what loads; the schema mirrors the keys testo_core/config/loader.py reads.
  2. scripts/export_config_schema.py writes it to schema/testosterone.schema.json. CI runs it with --check, the same way export_openapi.py guards frontend/openapi.json. Editors load it from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/taltal-beep/testosterone/main/schema/testosterone.schema.json.
  3. testo config init and testo init write the $schema line at the top of the file, and the repo's own configs point at the file by relative path.
  4. equipment, framework and reporter type suggest the built-in names but accept any string, because plugins add their own. Unknown keys on the top level, defaults, cycles and stages are errors, which is what catches typos. Reporter entries allow any key, since those are reporter options.
  5. Only the canonical cycles: layout is described. Legacy plans: and runs: still load, but the schema flags them.

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
• Generate from the dataclasses. Rejected: the dataclasses are the loaded form, not the YAML. YAML has equipment, if and args as a string or list; the dataclasses have framework, if_expr and a tuple.
  • Switch the loader to Pydantic and use its schema. Rejected for now: a rewrite of the loader for a small editor feature.
  • Submit to SchemaStore. Tried and declined for now: SchemaStore/schemastore#6546 (2026-10-24) was closed by a maintainer, who said space in the catalog is limited and to open a new PR once the tool is widely used. A duplicate opened by mistake on 2026-10-26 (#6552) was closed the same day. Until then, editors need the $schema line, which testo config init and testo init already write.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A new loader key needs a matching schema entry. tests/contract/testo_core/test_config_json_schema.py validates the repo's configs and the starter template against the schema, checks a set of invalid configs are flagged, and fails if the committed file is stale.
  • The schema URL follows main, so a key added on main shows up in editors before it is on PyPI.

docs.title: Delta Comparison Policy
docs.text: This document defines deterministic semantics for Phase 3 delta analytics.

docs.title: Run role semantics
docs.text:
• baseline_run_id: reference run used as the comparison anchor.
  • current_run_id: run being evaluated against baseline.
  • Delta formula:
  • absolute_delta = current_value - baseline_value
  • relative_delta_pct = ((current_value - baseline_value) / baseline_value) * 100 when baseline is non-zero.

docs.title: Classification labels
docs.text:
• improvement: metric moved in a favorable direction.
  • regression: metric moved in an unfavorable direction.
  • neutral: no change (absolute_delta == 0), or a duration change within timing noise (see below).
  • unknown: metric cannot be compared due to missing or incompatible data.

docs.title: Direction policy table
docs.text: Metric Group Better Direction Notes total_tests reliability higher More executed tests means broader reliability signal. passed reliability higher More passing tests is better. failed reliability lower More failed tests is worse. broken reliability lower More broken tests is worse. skipped reliability lower More skipped tests is treated as worse coverage quality. health_pct reliability higher Higher health percentage is better. wall_duration_ms performance lower Lower wall-clock duration is better. metrics_duration_ms performance lower Lower aggregate metrics duration is better. avg_case_ms performance lower Lower average case duration is better.

docs.title: Timing noise (added 2026-10-25)
docs.text: Two identical runs never take exactly the same time, so a duration metric (unit: ms) is only a regression or an improvement when the change is at least 5 % of the baseline and at least the metric's floor: 100 ms for wall_duration_ms and metrics_duration_ms, 5 ms for avg_case_ms. A smaller change is neutral with reason within_noise; its absolute_delta and relative_delta_pct are still reported, and Compare shows it as "Within noise". The dashboard's duration trend uses the same rule (delta_service.within_noise, 100 ms floor) and reads "flat". Test counts and health have no noise floor: one more failed test is always a regression. The constants are NOISE_RELATIVE_PCT and _MetricPolicy.noise_floor_ms in testo_core/services/delta_service.py.

docs.title: Unknown/null reason codes
docs.text:
• missing_current_metric: current run has no value.
  • missing_baseline_metric: baseline run has no value.
  • zero_baseline_for_relative: absolute delta can be computed, relative percent cannot.
  • incompatible_test_kind: run pair has different test_kind.
  • within_noise: not unknown, but the reason a neutral duration is neutral despite a non-zero delta.

docs.title: Stage-level deltas (added 2026-07-23)
docs.text: GET /api/v1/analytics/delta also returns stage_deltas: one entry per stage name present on either run's stage_health, matched by name (no archive extraction — reuses the stage_health already loaded on each CompletedRunView). Classification uses the same higher_is_better rule as health_pct above, applied to each stage's own health_pct. A stage present on only one side (renamed/added/removed since the baseline ran) gets classification: "unknown" with the missing side's fields null, rather than being dropped — mirrors the metric-level missing_*_metric reasons in spirit, but stage deltas don't carry a reason field.

docs.title: Per-test deltas (added 2026-07-23)
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/analytics/delta/cases returns the full per-test breakdown — the API/UI equivalent of testo diff's non---metrics-only output. Each test case is matched across the two runs by historyId → fullName → uuid (first present, in that order) and classified as:

  • added: present in current, not in baseline.
  • removed: present in baseline, not in current.
  • regression: passed in baseline → failed/broken in current.
  • fix: failed/broken in baseline → passed in current.
  • status_change: any other status transition.
  • (unchanged cases are computed but dropped from the response — only actual changes are returned.)

Unlike the run/stage-level deltas, this is computed on demand from each run's live artifact snapshot every request, with no caching — see CLI-UI Parity - Pyramid, Graphs, Deep Diff - 2026-07-23 for why (archives aren't large enough yet to justify the cache-invalidation work) and for why this reads from each run's snapshot directory rather than the separate ReportArchive table (testo report list/diff's id space, which has no link to run-history run ids).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: After the first PyPI release (1.1.1) the docs were only readable as markdown on GitHub, in the generated wiki, or in Obsidian. None of them is searchable or has a page a new user can start from, and the README's quickstart stopped at testo run without saying how to see a regression or add CI.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• A Getting Started note walks a new user from pip install testo-core to the GitHub Action. Every command in it was run against the PyPI release. examples/getting-started/ is the same project, and the getting_started job in ci.yml runs it through ./integrations/github-action on every pull request, so the guide fails CI when it stops working.
  • MkDocs Material renders docs/ as a site (mkdocs.yml), published under /docs/ of the existing Pages demo by pages-demo.yml: https://taltal-beep.github.io/testosterone/docs/. One Pages deployment keeps one URL to share and no second workflow writing to Pages.
  • The notes don't change for the site. scripts/mkdocs_hooks.py bridges the gaps at build time: Index.md becomes the home page, URLs are lowercase and hyphenated, the vault's status key is dropped (Material would show it as a badge on every page), and links that leave docs/ point at GitHub, the same rewrite the wiki export does. Anchors use GitHub's slug rules, so links written for GitHub resolve on the site.
  • Broken links fail CI. The docs_site job runs mkdocs build --strict. Archive/ is built but kept out of the navigation.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The vault now has three readers (GitHub, the wiki, the site) and one source. A new note needs a nav entry in mkdocs.yml to show in the site's menu; without one it is still built and searchable.
  • pip install -e ".[docs]" then mkdocs serve previews the site locally.
  • Material 9.x pins MkDocs below 2.0, which drops plugins and themes. The docs extra pins mkdocs-material<10 until that settles.
  • Mermaid diagrams render in the browser from a CDN script Material loads.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The project's notes existed in three places that drifted apart: docs/ in the repo, an Obsidian vault on the owner's machine (a shortcut to docs/ of a local clone that nobody pulled), and a GitHub wiki that was copied by hand once and had not changed since 2026-06-24. Notes used [[wikilinks]] that did not render on GitHub, had no metadata, and nothing checked them. AI agents working on the repo had no rule telling them to read or update the notes.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Introduced in #86, on top of the vault restructure in #74:

Change Where docs/ is the one source; the vault and the wiki are views of it Vault schema § Sync A schema for the vault: layers, frontmatter, writing rules, ingest / query / lint / log Vault schema Frontmatter (type, status, created, updated) on every note; append-only log every note scripts/docs_vault.py lint checks frontmatter, broken links, wikilinks, orphans and stale updated dates; runs in CI and as a contract test scripts/docs_vault.py, tests/contract/testo_core/test_docs_vault.py .github/workflows/wiki-sync.yml regenerates the wiki from docs/ on every push to main that touches the vault CI-CD Pipeline Setup Six "second brain" rules in the root CLAUDE.md: vault first, docs in sync, point don't paste, architectural consistency, document significant work, archive don't rewrite CLAUDE.md

The wiki export flattens note paths into page names (Specs & ADRs/README.md becomes Specs-and-ADRs), rewrites note links to wiki pages, and rewrites links to anything else in the repo, images included, to GitHub URLs on main. Mermaid blocks pass through unchanged and render in all three views.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Never edit the wiki: the next sync overwrites it.
  • The local Obsidian vault shows only what its clone has pulled. Run git pull --ff-only origin main in that clone, or let the Obsidian Git plugin pull on a timer (pull only, no commit or push).
  • Images must be committed under docs/assets/ and embedded from a note to appear in the vault and the wiki. Until 2026-10-08 the architecture diagram was embedded only in the root README.md, so it showed on GitHub but not in Obsidian or the wiki; System Diagram fixed that.
  • A pull request that edits a note without bumping its updated date fails CI, unless the note is already dated that day.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: testo flaky finds tests whose outcome keeps flipping (see Open Source Features - 2026-10-19), but finding them doesn't stop them from turning a pull request red. Tools teams adopt for flaky tests (Trunk, Datadog Test Optimization) let you quarantine a test: it keeps running and reporting, but it no longer fails the build while someone fixes it. This was gap 7 in the mainstream adoption review.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Config. A quarantine: list in testosterone.yaml, at the top level (every cycle) and per cycle (added to the top-level list). An entry is a test name glob, or {test, reason, owner}. Unknown keys are rejected. Parsed into QuarantineRule on Plan.quarantine (testo_core/config/). See QA Strategies for the YAML.
  2. Matching. fnmatch (case-sensitive) against the test's Allure name and fullName. So test_checkout* covers parametrized cases, and tests.api#* or payout rules.* (JUnit classname.name) covers a module or suite.
  3. Gate, in the executor. After the post-stage hooks, when the plan has rules and the process exited 1, testo_core/engine/quarantine.py reads the stage's *-result.json files. If there is at least one failed or broken test and all of them match, the stage's returncode becomes 0 and waived_returncode keeps the 1. Exit codes, --fail-fast and every consumer then see a passed stage without any change to them.
  4. Still reported. The result files aren't touched, so the failures count in health %, totals, Allure, Compare and flaky detection as before. StageResult.quarantined lists the matched tests and travels to run.log, the CLI summary (PASS (1 quarantined)), --ci NDJSON, events.ndjson, plan_result.json, the run record's stage metadata and testo report markdown (✅ pass · 1 quarantined, failing tests marked (quarantined)).
  5. testo flaky reads the cycle's rules (auto-discovered config, or --config), marks quarantined tests, prints a quarantine: snippet for the others, and --fail-on-flaky only counts unquarantined ones.

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
• Deselect quarantined tests (--deselect, -k "not ..."). Rejected: the test stops running, so there's no signal for when it's fixed, and every runner needs its own syntax.
  • Waive any exit code when all failures are quarantined. Rejected: pytest exits 2 for collection errors and 124/127 mean timeout and missing binary. Those failures have no per-test result to match, so only exit 1 ("tests ran, some failed") can be waived.
  • A separate quarantine.yaml or a database list edited from the UI. Deferred: the list belongs in code review next to the cycle it affects. A UI or API to add entries can come later and write the same YAML.
  • Rewrite quarantined results to skipped. Rejected: it would hide the failure from history, Compare and flaky detection.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A quarantined test can fail forever without anyone noticing unless they read the reports. reason and owner exist so the list documents who is fixing what; an expiry date is a possible follow-up.
  • A stage whose runner exits 1 without writing per-test results (no Allure output, no junit_xml) can't be waived: no failed tests are found, so the stage still fails.
  • The API and UI don't show quarantine yet (the stage metadata has it, but StageHealth in the OpenAPI schema doesn't expose it).
  • Tests: tests/unit/testo_core/test_quarantine.py (config, matching, the gate through a real command stage and run_plan), test_cli_flaky.py and test_run_summary_markdown.py.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Paid Features to Offer Free - 2026-10-31 ranked twelve features that competitors keep behind a paid plan. On 2026-11-01 Taltal picked five to build: F1 coverage history and coverage on the pull request comment, F2 a weekly digest, F5 hiding secrets before anything is stored, F6 backup and restore, and F9 previous failures first. The note's rules apply: only the ideas are copied, never code, assets or the competitors' feature names.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Each feature uses the paths that already exist. There is no new service and no new table, and every feature except redaction is off until asked for.

docs.title: F5: secrets hidden before a run is stored
docs.text:
testo_core/security/redaction.py used to clean only what went to the AI. redact_run_artifacts() now rewrites the text files a run wrote (.json, .xml, .log, .txt, .html, .trx, ... up to 50 MB; binaries, symlinks and non-UTF-8 files are left alone). run_plan() calls it once, after the last stage and before persistence. So testo run, testo ingest, POST /api/v1/ingest and pytest --testo are all covered, and reporters only see the cleaned files.

  • The built-in patterns cover private key blocks, sk-…, api_key=/token=/secret=, password=, Bearer …, AWS AKIA…/ASIA…, Google AIza…, GitHub ghp_…/github_pat_…, GitLab glpat-…, Slack xox…- tokens and hook URLs, JWTs, and user:password@ in URLs (scheme and host are kept).
  • The value patterns stop at quotes and backslashes, so a rewritten JSON file stays valid.
  • TESTO_REDACT_PATTERNS adds your own regular expressions, one per line. An invalid one is skipped with a warning. TESTO_REDACT=0 turns redaction off.
  • It is on by default: a secret in stored history is worse than a few ***REDACTED*** in a log.

docs.title: F6: testo backup and testo restore
docs.text:
testo_core/history/backup.py writes one .tar.gz containing a manifest, one JSONL file per table (read through SQLAlchemy) and the run snapshots under static/history/.

  • Because the tables are JSONL rather than a database dump, one backup moves between SQLite, Postgres and MySQL. The note had proposed a file copy plus pg_dump; this works for every database the project supports.
  • Values that aren't JSON are tagged ($dt, $date, $uuid, $b64), and enums are stored by name.
  • Restore refuses a database that already has runs unless --replace is given. It writes only the columns today's tables have, so an older backup still restores.
  • Archive members are checked before extraction (no absolute paths, no ..).
  • The AI settings file is never included. The manifest notes that user_account holds password hashes.

docs.title: F9: pytest --testo-failed-first
docs.text:
services/failed_first.py ranks each test from the cycle's history:

  1. failed in the last run;
  2. flaky;
  3. failed in one of the last 20 runs;
  4. everything else.

The pytest plugin then does a stable sort, after --testo-affected and --testo-shard. History is read the same way --testo-shard reads it (services/test_split.load_test_items): locally, or from /api/v1/analytics/tests with --testo-server. That makes the order the team's history, not one machine's cache. The pytest-xdist controller loads the ranks once and passes them to each worker through workerinput. If no history can be read, pytest's own order is kept and the summary line says why.

docs.title: F2: testo notify --digest week|day
docs.text:
services/run_digest.py builds one message per period from the stored runs and their snapshots. For each cycle it shows:

  • runs and green builds, against the period before;
  • test pass rate and line coverage, against the period before;
  • tests that turned flaky (flaky_service.classify, the same rule as testo flaky);
  • tests still failing;
  • tests fixed since the previous period's last run;
  • the five tests that got slower (median passed time, above the 20 ms noise floor).

It is sent as Slack Block Kit or a Teams Adaptive Card to the webhooks the per-run alerts already use. Testosterone has no scheduler, so a cron line or a scheduled CI job runs it. A period with no runs sends nothing.

docs.title: F1: coverage with each run and on the pull request comment
docs.text:
reporting/coverage_import.py recognises a report by its content, as the result importers do: Cobertura XML, JaCoCo XML (the report's LINE counter), LCOV (LF/LH), and Go cover profiles (statements, with blocks repeated across test binaries counted once). Several reports are added together. DTDs are stripped and entities are refused.

How coverage gets in:

  • testo run --coverage FILE reads the file after the stages finish. A missing file only logs a warning, so a crashed test run is still recorded.
  • testo ingest --coverage FILE checks the file before recording, so a typo is exit 2.
  • The GitHub Action has a coverage input.

Where it is kept and shown:

  • Only the totals are stored, as coverage_pct, coverage_covered and coverage_total in the run record's metadata, the same place CI provenance goes.
  • With --server, the client sends the covered and total counts. The server checks them and computes the percentage itself.
  • CompletedRunView and GET /api/v1/runs/{id} expose the three numbers, and the run page shows them.
  • testo report markdown (job summary and PR comment) adds coverage 81.2% (▼ 0.4) against the same baseline as its test changes, and the digest adds it per cycle.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The five features are free and need no new service. Redaction is the only behaviour change for existing users. It changes stored files, never test outcomes, and TESTO_REDACT=0 restores the old behaviour.
  • F1 is narrower than the note's sketch. There is no per-file coverage and no coverage trend chart on the cycle page yet. The stored per-run totals are what such a chart would read, and diff coverage (changed lines only) can follow on top of what testo affected knows about changed files.
  • Coverage lives in run metadata rather than a column. That fits the current read side; it moves to a real column with the rest when the database migrations planned in the architecture review land.
  • Redaction patterns are a best effort. A secret in an unusual shape still needs TESTO_REDACT_PATTERNS.
  • Restoring a big history goes through the ORM in batches of 500 rows. That is slower than a native dump, but works the same on every database.

Builds on Alerts Where Developers Look - 2026-10-22, Ingest and Team Server - 2026-10-22 and Affected Test Selection - 2026-10-30.

docs.title: GitHub Action PR Comment - 2026-10-19
docs.text: Part of the post-publish feature batch (Specs & ADRs).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The GitHub Action exposed the final plan_finished event as step outputs and nothing else. To see what failed, a reviewer had to open the job log and read NDJSON. Other test reporters for CI post a summary where reviewers already look: the job summary and the pull request.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• The text is a core feature, not action code. testo report markdown (testo_core/services/run_summary_markdown.py) renders a stored run: counts, a per-stage table, failing tests, and per-test changes since the cycle's previous run, reusing the per-test diff Compare uses. Anything (GitLab, a script) can call it; the action is one caller.
  • Job summary on by default, PR comment opt in. Writing $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY needs no permission. Commenting needs pull-requests: write, so it is comment-on-pr: "true".
  • One comment per cycle, edited in place. The Markdown starts with <!-- testo-summary:<cycle> -->; the action looks for a comment starting with it and edits that instead of posting a new one on every push. Two cycles in one workflow get two comments.
  • Never changes the result. Rendering or commenting failures (a fork's read-only token, an API error) are ::warning:: lines; the step keeps testo run's exit code. Standard library only (urllib), so the action adds no dependency.
  • package input. The action pip-installs testo-core by default; package: . installs a checkout. This repository's github_action CI job uses that to run the action on its own code and comment on its own pull requests, while getting_started keeps testing the PyPI release.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• "Since the previous run" needs history from an earlier job. On a fresh runner the first summary says there is nothing to compare with; caching testo_history.db or a shared database.url fixes that. The CI job runs the cycle twice to exercise the comparison.
  • The comment and the job summary describe the latest run of the cycle in the database the action sees, which is the run it just made.

docs.title: Human-Run Resource Provider - 2026-10-30
docs.text: Index · Shared Resource Pools · Resource Lifecycle Hooks - 2026-10-26

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Resource Lifecycle Hooks left a "provider" (create, reset, check, destroy, list) and dynamic pools as options. The owner's rule for them: Testosterone must never create or delete VMs on its own. Pools stay fixed lists of keys in testosterone.yaml; the only automatic commands are the user's own hooks, which reset or check a key that already exists.

What a provider still adds under that rule: seeing whether a pool matches the real VMs (keys that vanished, leftovers outside the pool), and later a safe, logged way for a person to add or remove VMs.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
A pool's provider: holds the user's own shell commands. Testosterone ships no VMware, cloud or hypervisor code and holds no credentials. Provider commands run only from testo pool, typed by a person, on that person's machine.

  1. Read-only status (pull request 206). provider.list prints the keys that exist. testo pool status [POOL] [--check] compares that with the pool, shows each key's lease state, and with --check runs the pool's existing on_check on free keys (a held key is never checked). It changes nothing: no disable, no lease, no command besides list and on_check. Exit 1 when a pool needs a look, so a CI schedule can warn.
  2. Never automatic, enforced. ResourcePool.to_json never includes provider, so it never reaches a team server or a stage's workers. tests/unit/testo_core/test_pool_provider.py fails if any module besides testo_core/cli/commands/pool.py imports testo_core.resources.provider.
  3. on_check is reused, not a second provider.check: one "is this key usable?" command, whether run on take or by testo pool status --check.
  4. Human-run changes. testo pool add / remove / sweep run the user's provider.create and provider.destroy:
    • a dry run unless --apply, which asks first unless --yes;
    • refused unless the verb is under provider.allow (which then needs list, name_prefix, and for create max_items), and when TESTO_PROVIDER_ACTIONS=0;
    • at most 5 keys per command; add stops at max_items (pool items plus what list shows);
    • destroy only on names with name_prefix that list shows, that nobody holds and that aren't in items;
    • nothing runs if list fails.
  5. Every command is logged. Table resource_action (pool, key, verb, user, host, command, ok, detail, time) in the lease database, or on the team server through POST /api/v1/resources/actions (a write: token or runner; the account name wins over the client's). GET /api/v1/resources/actions, testo pool log and a "Provider commands" card on the Resources page show it. If logging fails, the command stops before running anything else.
  6. The config stays the source of truth. add never edits testosterone.yaml; the person adds new keys to items, and takes a key out of items before removing it.

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
• Stop at fixed pools (no provider). Safe, but drift and leftovers stay invisible until a test fails on a missing VM.
  • Automatic dynamic pools (create when the pool runs dry, destroy when a lease ends). This is how Testcontainers and cloud autoscalers work. Rejected: it breaks the owner's rule even if off by default, and brings quotas, cost and orphan handling.
  • A Python provider class (provider: module:Class). Possible later under the same rules; shell commands cover the users today.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Nothing changes for a pool without provider:. testo pool status on such a pool shows lease states and ? for existence.
  • A failing provider.list is reported (exit 3), never guessed from: existence shows ?.
  • Leftovers are only reported by status. Removing them is a person's job: their own scripts, or testo pool sweep --apply.
  • Adding a VM is two steps (testo pool add --apply, then add it to items). That is on purpose: no key enters or leaves a pool without a person.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The result importers (Runner Coverage - 2026-10-26) and the integrations around a run (the GitHub Action, the PR comment, Slack/Teams alerts, OpenTelemetry export, affected-test selection, the plugin API) are where Testosterone meets files and services it doesn't control. This hunt fed them:

  • more than 60 malformed and edge-case files: empty, truncated, UTF-16, BOM, billion-laughs, XXE, inf/nan times, wrong field types, 2 MB messages, HTML error pages;
  • reports written by the real tools in the cloud container: Go 1.24.7 (go test -json: build failure, panic, -timeout), Jest 29, jest-junit, Vitest 3, Playwright 1.48, RSpec 3.13 and Robot Framework 7.

It looked for crashes, wrong counts and silent data loss. The integrations were checked with local stubs only: no real Slack, Teams or OTLP endpoint.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Small, safe fixes shipped with tests, one pull request per area. Bigger items are proposals below and wait for a decision.

docs.title: Findings, ranked
docs.text: Status: fixed means merged or in an open fix PR (number given). proposal means not started.

docs.title: High
docs.text: # Area Finding Status H1 Go Go 1.24+ reports a build failure as build-output events keyed by ImportPath before any Package event. The importer rejected the whole file as "not valid JSON", so testo ingest recorded 0 tests and exited 0 for every Go build failure. fixed #217 H2 testo ingest A truncated, empty or non-report file (a job killed mid-write) recorded a passing run with 0 tests (exit 0). fixed #217: exits 1 when nothing was readable H3 Playwright A spec that doesn't compile, or a failing globalSetup, stops Playwright before any test runs. The failure only appears in top-level errors, so the run was 0 tests, exit 0. fixed #217: one broken result per error H4 Jest/Vitest A beforeAll/afterAll that throws fails the file. The tests show passed (Jest) or skipped (Vitest), so the run was green. fixed #217: (test file failed) broken result H5 PR comment A backtick in a test name closed the code span, so @user/@org/team pings and raw HTML rendered live. In a fork PR the author controls test names. fixed #226

docs.title: Medium
docs.text: # Area Finding Status M1 All importers One file with an unexpected field type (non-dict Jest/Playwright entries, a non-string error.message, RSpec pending_message, k6 passes, JUnit time="inf") crashed the whole import. Every other file's results were lost: testo ingest exited 4 with a traceback, and the post-stage hook logged "import failed". fixed #232 M2 TRX A crashed test host (RunInfo outcome="Error") with no results was recorded as passed. fixed #217 M3 JUnit A <testsuite errors="1"> with no failing <testcase> (a suite that failed to load) counted as passed. fixed #217 M4 Go A test that hit -timeout was dropped, and only "(package failed)" showed. fixed #217: the hung test is broken M5 Robot A failed suite teardown didn't fail the suite's tests. output.xml keeps each test's PASS, and robot applies "Parent suite teardown failed" when it reads the file, so robot exited 2 while Testosterone recorded 1 failure. fixed #232 M6 JUnit A <testsuite> nested under a root <testsuite> was read as 0 tests, and UTF-16 XML (the Windows PowerShell default) was rejected. fixed #232 M7 PR comment With no target-branch run, the baseline fell back to the newest run on any branch. A push to main was compared with a feature branch, and a PR with another PR. fixed #226 M8 Action When testo run stopped before recording a run (bad config), the Action published the previous job's run (restored from cache) as this job's summary, comment, annotations and alert. summary_json never carried the error. fixed #226 M9 Plugins One reporter plugin that failed to import turned off every reporter, including Slack, Teams and Allure. PluginError is a ValueError, and the orchestrator swallowed it. fixed #229 M10 Plugins A constructor that raised crashed testo run after the cycle had finished and turned a green exit 0 into 1. fixed #229 M11 Affected A folder rule (tests/payments/**) also picked __init__.py and helpers, so pytest --testo-affected always ran everything. fixed #229 M12 Affected git quotes non-ASCII paths, so tests/test_é.py was never selected. fixed #229

docs.title: Low
docs.text:
# Area Finding Status L1 JUnit Maven Surefire reruns (flakyFailure, rerunFailure) passed without the flaky flag. fixed #232 L2 JUnit A report whose name contains -attachment (email-attachment-tests.xml) was skipped as an Allure attachment. fixed #232 L3 JUnit An HTML error page or other non-JUnit XML counted 0 tests with no warning. fixed #232 L4 JUnit The message attribute wasn't capped (2 MB stored whole). fixed #232 L5 Summary "No test changed outcome" was shown when the previous run had no stored results. fixed #226 L6 Summary The runner column wasn't escaped, a cycle name with --> ended the comment marker, and list items showed \|. fixed #226 L7 pytest JUnit A test that passes and then errors in teardown is written as two <testcase> entries with the same name, so it counts as 2 tests (1 passed, 1 broken). fixed (P3) L8 Go With -count=2, or reruns in one file, attempts of the same test overwrite each other, so a fail-then-pass test isn't flagged flaky. fixed (P3) L9 Action cycle: all publishes the summary, annotations and alert of the last cycle only. fixed (P4) L10 Action ${{ inputs.* }} are pasted into the composite step's bash, so a " or $(…) in an input (cycle: ${{ github.head_ref }}) runs as shell. fixed (P5) L11 OTel test.case.name is the same for every parametrized case, and an endpoint with no scheme exits 3 instead of 2. fixed (P6) L12 JUnit A suite's tests="5" with only 1 <testcase> gives no warning, and a naive timestamp is read as local time. count warning added (P2); naive timestamps stay local time, which is what pytest and Surefire write

Suspected, not verified: - Teams card text isn't markdown-escaped (_x_ turns italic). - Slack's 3,000-character cut can split an &. - upsert_pr_comment edits the first comment carrying the marker, whoever wrote it. - A plugin raising SystemExit at import isn't caught. - A "(quarantined)" tag is lost on names over 120 characters.

Belongs to the engine/CLI hunt instead: Playwright JSON with a BOM, report paths containing [ ], environment.xml outside Allure folders, testcases directly under <testsuites>, and xcresult 1.2.3s durations.

Checked and fine: - Billion-laughs and XXE are refused by expat. - Playwright attachment paths outside the repo (/etc/passwd, ../..) are never copied. - Slack/Teams with bad URLs become AlertError, and the URL never leaks. - Slack escapes <!channel>. - OTLP refused, 500 and wrong-path responses exit 3, and a missing [otel] extra exits 2 with a hint. - RSpec errors outside examples (load errors, after(:context) failures) are already a broken result. - The GitHub comment size limit can't be hit (names are cut to 120 characters, lists to 20 rows). - A fork's read-only token only warns.

docs.title: Proposals
docs.text:
• P1. Prefer runners' own formats over jest-junit. In real output, jest-junit (default config) dropped a test file that failed to compile and named every suite undefined. The Getting Started and setup prompts could say "use jest --json" first. Docs only. Done 2026-11-01: README, Getting Started, Team Server and Command Reference now show jest --json.
  • P2. Cross-check suite counts. When a <testsuite tests="N"> claims more cases than it holds, log a warning like the Playwright report notes. This is cheap, but some tools write wrong counts, so warn rather than fail.
  • P3. Merge duplicate attempts. Fold same-name <testcase> entries in one suite (the pytest teardown error) and repeated Go runs into one result: worst status wins, and a fail followed by a pass is flaky. This changes counts users already have, so it needed a decision. Decided 2026-11-01 (Taltal: go with the recommendation), built: see Decision on duplicate attempts.
  • P4. cycle: all in the Action. Publish one summary and alert per plan_finished event.
  • P5. Action inputs through env:. Read inputs as environment variables in the composite steps instead of ${{ }} in bash. Also split package on spaces so testo-core pytest-xdist works.
  • P6. OTel naming. Use the test's parametrized name in test.case.name, and treat an endpoint with no scheme as bad input (exit 2).

docs.title: Decision on duplicate attempts (2026-11-01)
docs.text:
Taltal approved P3 as recommended. A test listed more than once in one JUnit <testsuite>, or run more than once in one go test -json file (-count=N), is now one result:

  • a failure followed by a final pass is passed and flaky, with the first failure's message ("Passed on rerun. …");
  • otherwise the worst attempt wins: failed, then broken, then passed, then skipped (a pass followed by a teardown error is broken).

The merge is by the test's history id (tool plus full name), only inside one suite or one Go file. The same name in two suites, two files or two Playwright projects stays separate. The other importers already report one result per test (Playwright and Jest keep retries inside the test).

What changes for users: totals for affected reports go down (pytest before 8 with teardown errors, go test -count), and a few tests that were counted as failed are now flaky passes. Old runs keep their stored counts. The shared helper is fold_attempts in testo_core/reporting/imported_results.py.

P2 shipped with it: a leaf <testsuite tests="N"> listing fewer than N cases adds a note to the import log ("the runner may have stopped while writing it"). It never fails the stage, because some tools write wrong counts.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A red build outside any single test now becomes a broken result and a red testo ingest. This adds results named (test file failed), (failed to load), (test run error), (suite failed) and (package failed), so totals can be one higher than the runner's own test count.
  • One bad file never costs the other files' results.
  • The fuzz harness and the real-tool reports are not checked in. The regression tests use the real tools' shapes, in tests/unit/testo_core/test_import_failures_not_green.py and test_import_hardening.py.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A review of what keeps Testosterone niche (2026-10-22) found that the tools teams actually adopt (ReportPortal, Currents, Trunk, Testmo) ask for one line in an existing CI job and give back one place the whole team looks at. Testosterone asked users to move their test commands into testosterone.yaml, and kept history in a SQLite file on one machine. In CI that file disappears with the runner. Two features close the gap: record results that some other step produced, and a server many CI jobs can record into.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. equipment: junit (testo_core/frameworks/junit_adapter.py). An adapter with runs_process = False. The executor (_record_junit_stage) skips the subprocess, imports the stage's junit_xml reports with the existing converter (reporting/junit_import.py), without the "newer than the stage" filter, and derives the returncode: 1 when a case failed or broke, or when nothing matched; 0 otherwise. Stage duration is the summed test time, and the plan's duration is the larger of the wall clock and the summed stage durations, so ingested runs have meaningful duration trends.
  2. testo ingest builds a one-stage junit cycle (cycle_run.junit_ingest_plan, strict name and pattern checks) and runs it through CycleRunService, like testo run. Exit codes follow the engine contract. No testosterone.yaml is needed (loader.load_config_or_defaults).
  3. POST /api/v1/ingest (testo_api/routes/ingest.py → services/junit_ingest.py) writes the uploaded files to a scratch directory and records them through the same service, one upload at a time (a process lock). The client's CI provenance is sent as form fields, because the server's own environment says nothing about the client's CI; it reaches the run record through a new CycleRunOptions.run_metadata → run_plan(run_metadata=) → PlanResult.extra["run_metadata"], merged last by the DB backend. Uploads are size-limited and never executed.
  4. testo ingest --server URL --token (services/ingest_client.py) uploads instead of recording locally, and exits with the server's result, or 3 when the upload fails.
  5. The API serves the UI when TESTO_UI_DIR points at a build (testo_api/ui.py, SPA fallback after all API routes). Same-origin writes are allowed only when TESTO_API_TOKEN is set, because a DNS-rebinding page is also "same origin".

  6. Dockerfile.testo-server (UI build + API with [api,db]) and deploy/server/docker-compose.yml (plus Postgres, token required). docker-publish.yml publishes testo-server next to testo-runner; the team_server CI job runs the compose file end to end.

  7. Lighter install (the third item of the same review). Behave, BehaveX and Allure-Behave move from the core dependencies to a bdd extra, so pip install testo-core for testo ingest or pytest/Playwright cycles pulls 35 packages instead of 47. The dev extra and the testo-runner image include bdd. A behave/behavex stage without it fails with rc 127 (exit 3), and the stage error, now shown in the CLI stage panel, names the extra. scripts/package_smoke.sh checks that a plain install has neither. The GitHub Action's package input and a new TESTO_PACKAGE variable in the GitLab template select the extra. The README and PyPI description now lead with what a run answers (what broke, what's flaky, what got slower) and with testo ingest.

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
• A separate ingest pipeline that writes run records directly. Rejected: a second path into history is what the Architecture Consolidation removed. Going through CycleRunService gives ingested runs reporters, snapshots, the report archive and metrics push for free.
  • Upload Allure results instead of JUnit. Deferred. Almost every runner writes JUnit XML; native formats (Playwright JSON) can be added as more runs_process = False parsers.
  • Accounts and projects on the server. Deferred. One token is enough to try it in a team, and it matches the existing TESTO_API_TOKEN model.
  • Ship the UI inside the PyPI wheel (testo ui). Still open. The server image covers the team case without growing the wheel.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• SUPPORTED_FRAMEWORKS gains junit. The ad-hoc run API doesn't offer it (it needs files, not a command).
  • New CLI command, API route, env var (TESTO_UI_DIR), Docker image and CI job; documented in Command Reference § testo ingest, Team Server, Publishing Docker Images, Architecture Overview and Deep Dive - Execution Logic.
  • Tests: tests/unit/testo_core/test_junit_ingest.py (config, plan validation, executor, run metadata, CLI) and tests/contract/api/test_ingest_contract.py (endpoint, token, limits, UI serving, same-origin rule, upload client).
  • The first testo-server push creates a private GHCR package that the owner makes public once.
  • Uploaded-only cycles don't appear on the Cycles page (it lists testosterone.yaml). Follow-up.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Ship the orchestrator as an installable library (testo-core on PyPI, import testo_core) so the CLI, CI wrappers, the API and custom scripts share one engine instead of each needing an app checkout.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
Item Location Package metadata pyproject.toml: name = "testo-core" Public API testo_core/__init__.py CLI entry testo console script (testo_core.cli.app:main) API entry testo-api console script (testo_api) Dev install pip install -e '.[dev]'

Run history is always saved (SQLite by default), so sqlmodel is a core dependency; the [db] extra only adds the Postgres driver and tomli-w. The package CI job installs the built wheel with no extras and runs a cycle to keep it that way.

An installed package writes nothing next to its own code: run data goes to <cwd>/.testo/ or $TESTO_HOME, and a source checkout keeps using the repository root (Architecture Overview § Artifact layout). Up to 1.1.1 it was always relative to the package directory, so a pip install wrote static/ into site-packages.

FastAPI (testo_api) and the React frontend are optional consumers: testo run must not need them. See Architecture Overview § Adjacent packages (same repo).

Publishing: Publishing to PyPI. Commands: Command Reference.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
After the first PyPI release (1.1.1) and the docs site, the owner chose to build "Tier 3" of the post-publish list: features that widen who can use Testosterone. Each lands as its own pull request; this note records the decisions behind them.

Feature State Flaky test detection This note, below PR comment from the GitHub Action GitHub Action PR Comment - 2026-10-19 Plugin API for framework adapters and reporters Plugin API - 2026-10-19 More framework adapters Playwright Adapter - 2026-10-19 GitLab mirror and CI template Needs the owner's GitLab account (GitLab Pages Demo)

docs.title: Flaky test detection
docs.text:
Decision. A test is flaky when, within the last window runs of one cycle (default 20), it both passed and failed and its outcome changed at least twice. Skipped and unknown runs neither pass nor fail. One change is a plain regression or fix, which Compare and testo summary already show; changing back and forth is what points at the test rather than the code. Results are ranked by flip rate (changes over observations minus one).

Where the data comes from. Each run record's own artifact snapshot (static/history/<run_id>/artifacts/, the Allure *-result.json files DbBackend copies per run), matched by historyId like the per-test diff. No schema change, and it works on every database backend.

One implementation, three surfaces. testo_core/services/flaky_service.py is called by testo flaky (Command Reference), GET /api/v1/analytics/flaky?cycle= and the Flaky tests card on the cycle page. The static export writes data/flaky/<cycle>.json, so the Pages demo shows the fake-api app's /api/flaky route flipping across runs.

Consequences. Reading every snapshot in the window is linear in runs times tests; fine at the default window, and the API caps window at 200. --fail-on-flaky lets CI gate on it, but in CI the history only spans runs that share a database or a cached history directory, as in the Pages workflow.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry Export - 2026-10-30
docs.text: Part of the mainstream-adoption work (Specs & ADRs).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Teams that already run Datadog, Grafana (Tempo), Honeycomb or Jaeger want test runs next to the services they test, in the tool they already open. All of them take OpenTelemetry traces over OTLP. Testosterone kept runs only in its own history and UI, and Compared With Other Tools told Datadog teams to look elsewhere.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• One trace per run. A root span for the run, a child span per stage, and a child span per test under its stage. Tests keep their real start and stop times from the stored results (Allure start / stop); a stage spans its tests, or is laid out from its recorded duration_s when it has none. Failed and broken tests, red stages and red runs get status ERROR, with the failure message on tests.
  • Built from run history. testo_core/services/otel_export.py reads the stored run (CompletedRunView) and its snapshot, so any recorded run can be sent: right after testo run by the otel reporter, or later by testo otel --cycle/--run-id (after testo ingest or pytest --testo too). This is the same split as the Slack and Teams alerts.
  • Attributes follow the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions where they exist (test.suite.name, test.suite.run.status, test.case.name, test.case.result.status, vcs.ref.head.name, vcs.ref.head.revision, vcs.ref.base.name), plus testo.* for the rest (run id, cycle, stage, framework, raw status, counts). service.name is testosterone unless service_name / --service-name or OTEL_SERVICE_NAME say otherwise.
  • Standard configuration. Endpoint, headers and protocol come from the usual OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* variables, so a collector already set up for the services works unchanged. The reporter can override them; testo otel takes --endpoint and --protocol but never headers, because they usually hold API keys (same rule as webhook URLs).
  • Off by default, optional dependency. Nothing is sent unless the otel reporter is configured or testo otel is run. The SDK and the OTLP/HTTP exporter are the [otel] extra, so pip install testo-core stays light. OTLP/gRPC needs opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc on top, since grpcio is heavy.
  • Errors are reported, not logged. Spans are collected in memory and exported in batches of 512, and a batch the collector refuses fails the reporter (or exits 3) instead of disappearing into a log line. The trace is built as plain data first, so --dry-run and the tests need no SDK.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Test runs show up in any OTLP backend as traces, searchable by run id, cycle, branch and commit. Slow tests are visible on a timeline; a failing test is an error span.
  • One trace per export: sending the same run twice gives two traces.
  • Not done: linking test spans to the traces of the service under test (that needs trace context propagated into the tests), metrics or logs over OTLP, and a "View trace" link in the UI.
  • Commands and options: Command Reference § testo otel.
